title: You get what you pay for!
text:
I went in knowing this was a 3 star hotel, but booked it because there were so many good reviews on trip advisor. Boy they had me fooled. 

This hotel is about 3 blocks from the nearest metro.  The neighborhood is definitely a bit seedy. At night there was really no where around that I was comfortable enough to have dinner. Breakfast options were no better. There was literally no good cafes around offering breakfast. There are 2 supermarkets within walking distance that you can grab a bite from.

The room was disappointing. There was a leak in the bathroom underneath the toilet, and the bathroom reeked of urine. The design of the room screamed hostel. The lobby area is below average, but there is a nice lounge where I ordered a tasty pizza and a bottle of rosé. The pizza and the rosé were the highlights of my thankfully only one night here. I didn’t utilize the buffet so I cannot rate it. The staff were just ok. Not overly friendly or welcoming. Upon check-in I was given one key. I asked for a second and was told sorry we only give out one. I have never visited a hotel that only gave out one key. This was my last night in Paris so I needed somewhere inexpensive to stay. While most of the nice hotels were going for 350+ Euro a night, I manage to snag this one for the low 100 range. Big mistake!  You get what you pay for. Do not stay here, even if only for one night, it is totally not worth it.

text:

Limited selection but quality was good. Would recommend trying it one morning at least.

Overall our stay was very pleasant and I would recommend the hotel to others.

title: Economical and Good Value in Paris
text: We stayed at the Hotel for 3 nights, as part of a family holiday.  We booked 2 rooms online and when we arrived, found the hotel personnel to be courteous and helpful as we had young children with us.  Although the rooms are not large, they are sufficient for overnight stays and very clean and comfortable.  The hotel amenities include a restaurant and lounge which has good food and reasonably priced drinks.  The location is about 20 minutes from the Paris sights and very easy to get to on the Metro which is a short walk from the hotel.  On our last day we had a bit of time to kill before catching our flight out so the hotel stored our luggage and we walked up the street to the Museum of Science and Industry, which was a fabulous day spent looking at some very interesting displays.  The area of La Villette is not great as there are a lot of very questionable people in the area, however, that is the reality of Paris.  The hotel is very safe and we are glad we chose this property.

title: Disappointed
text: Their thumbnail picture in TripAdvisor is misleading or totally wrong.  This hotel is not in the best part of town and does not have pleasant views.  We stayed 6 days, and I can't tell where the picture is from.  It is a picture from an isolated courtyard at best.  The view from our room was directly into some sketchy apartments, and the main entrance is on a main/busy street.  There might have been a few trees on the other side of the street, and the median was mostly paved so vendors could set up their tents.  We did not feel totally safe walking around outside when it was getting dark/later as more people who looked questionable were just loitering in various places.  Consequently, we made it a point to be back by a certain time each day.  Hotel food was the worst food we ate in Paris and on our entire 2 week trip to Europe.  After the bad lunch we never ate there again.  We did like that the hotel was a brief 4 minute, direct walk from a metro stop and that you needed to use your room card to use the elevator.  The staff was okay.  The room was clean yet worn and small.  The shelving/cubbies were helpful to keep our suitcases accessible and not on the floor.  Beds were super low to the ground and not comfortable.  The shower tub was unusually high to step in/out of.  Plenty of space for toiletries in the bathroom counter.

title: Meets criteria for budget hotel with access to the city centre
text:
Good hotel for those on a budget, needing to just stay somewhere in Paris with close proximity to a metro (Crimee was a 3-4 minute walk) through which they can go into the city. Good for a family of 4, as they have a room with 2 double beds and 2 single beds.

Amenities were sparse, as in, no safe or fridge and an open-style cupboard. Not a complaint, but you get what you pay for (except in Asia, for the price, you would get a 4-star, and this was more like a 3-star).

The downside was that the toilet area was separate from the sink and shower area, and not even next door, but a few steps away through the room. And the toilet area had a certain smell to it.

The area seemed a bit shady, but it had restaurants, grocery stores and some hustle and bustle. A few minutes drive from Gare Du Nord, so convenient if you're coming or going from the Eurostar.

The staff was very courteous, so no issues there. If the goal is to visit Paris, spend the whole day out, and only need a place to sleep, for 2-4 people, this should be quite sufficient.

title: No Complaints About this Budget-Friendly Hotel
text:
We have just come back from a 4 night stay at Campanile 19 La Villette, and I can only give praise in this review.

Firstly, all staff were great with us and patient with our basic grasp of French. All staff we encountered during our stay were fabulous; always pleasant, friendly and helpful. A special mention must go to a particularly friendly staff member in the restuarant who shared jokes with us, boxed our left over pizza for the following day's lunch (the pizzas are excellent!), and got us a free glass of bubbly each when we told him that we had got that day.

Rooms are small but clean and modern with a good shower in the ensuite. Perfectly manageable size for a short stay. Crimèe and Corentin Cariou metro stations (line 7) are a couple of minutes walk away, meaning easy journeys to all of Paris.

Rooms on the rear of the hotel are quieter as Avenue de Flandre is a busy road out front.

Highly recommend a stay here.

title: Excellent buffet options, location and staff
text:
Chose this hotel from Tripadvisor reviews. We were very pleased to stay here. Why?
LOCATION: Conveniently between 2 Metro (subway) stations, however, it is somewhat closer to Corentin Cariou Metro. Two grocery stores are within view of the front entrance; one grocery store beside the hotel and the other across the street.
MEALS: rather than search for places to have our meals, we opted for breakfasts and suppers on-site. The breakfast buffet was 10.90 Euros with a satisfying variety of hot and cold foods. One of the best varieties I have seen in a long time for a hotel breakfast buffet. The suppers offered menu meals, but we preferred the "Buffet des entrées" at 11.90 Euros which included the salad bar, charcuterie, salsa, grilled chicken etc. More than enough for us. My husband liked that the restaurant was clean, friendly and a "guaranteed" good experience with friendly/efficient staff. 
STAFF: went out of their way to be friendly and helpful. In fact, our entire stay in Paris, we never met any of the "snobbishness" that Parisians used to have. We found the front desk bent over backwards to help us when we got our power adaptor stuck in the wall plug.
ROOM: was very functional, clean with modern colours. I can understand how people find it small if they have big suitcases and/or tend to spread out all over the room when they travel. My husband and I routinely travel with only a carry-on each for our clothing (I've done 3 weeks, twice, this way), so we did not find the room too small for our use.
[Cultural warning -- nothing to do with the hotel itself: as Canadians, we showed up for supper at 6 pm, but the restaurant was nowhere ready to open, Parisians dine much later. We just came back later.]

title: Can’t fault this for a budget hotel
text:
We stayed here on our first night in Paris. I loved  how the hotel is situated in a more residential than tourist area as it gave us a more authentic feel of the city. There is a supermarket next door to the hotel and plenty of boulangeries and patisseries with delicious pastries, bread and cakes nearby. There are three metro stations closeby - Corentin Cariou, Crimee and another I can’t remember the name of. We got the train from Charles de Gaulle to Gare du Nord and thereafter the metro to Stalingrad then on to Corentin Cariou which is a few minutes walk from the hotel. I would recommend downloading the metro app and using it to get around. A day pass for Zone1 covers all the tourist attractions and cost 7.5 euros and can be used as many times as you want that day. A single is around 1.9 euros. 

The hotel is located close to the canal which is definitely worth a visit. There are some lovely cafes and restaurants nearby as well as picnic spots. You can buy a bottle of wine and nibbles from the supermarket and enjoy the atmosphere at the canal in the evenings. As two female travellers we felt safe in this area and had no concerns. 

Check in was quick and easy. We paid for the room on check in and the staff were friendly and welcoming and spoke English as well as several other languages. 

You are given a key card for your room which is also needed to activate the lifts which was a good security feature. 

I note the other reviewers state the rooms are small however for a short stay they were perfectly fine. We used the room as a base to sleep and shower. Our room had two single beds with a space between them and there was more than enough space to walk around the room. There is no wardrobe however there is a rail with some hangers and a large drawer. This can be seen on the images when booking the hotel so there should be no surprises there. There is also a kettle and some tea and coffee in the room. There is also a tv however we didn’t use this. 

The bathroom was also fine. There is a bath with two shower attachments. The fixed shower had great water pressure. There was also some shower gel in a dispenser on the wall as well as some other small toiletries. Towels were included in the room. 

Overall this hotel was great value for money and is not close to the tourist attractions other than the Sacre Coeur however I preferred this as it was really easy to get around using the metro and prices in the area were reasonable. 

I would definitely use this hotel as base on my next trip to Paris.

title: Budget hotel but nice stay
text:
Very easy to find, located next to a supermarkets and close to a metro line. 
Lots of cafes around and within walking distance to the main attractions (depending on fitness levels) Eiffel Tower is about a 40 min walk. Public transport is really cheap tho approx 1,70€ for a day ticket. 

The staff are friendly and speak about 5 different languages well. They have free luggage storage if you arrive before check in. You can add breakfast for 10,90€ per person per night. It's made up of 3 cereals,   Yoghurt, milk, fruit, cheese, ham, chocolate crossiants, breads, cakes, spreads, scrambled eggs, sausages, juice, tea selection and coffee machine. 

The rooms are on the small side but they are perfect for what you need them for, clean, the beds are not the comfiest as you can feel the springs but you can still sleep. They have air con, a tv and a kettle. 

Wifi is free and works well. I had to log back in each time we came back from being out but that's no issue. 

All in all this was a good stay in Paris, it's a little on the pricy side for what you get but hey that's Paris . 

Warning however if you use booking.com they have a no cancelation, and you can't modify your booking or they will charge you the entire rate of your stay regardless. We had an emergency and had to cancel 2 of our nights which they didn't assist us in anyway, the hotel didn't even email me back which was quite disappointing.  It does state it on bookings.com but a bit of empathy never goes astray.

title: 3 Night stay to see Coldplay
text:
This is an excellent hotel to stay if you are on a budget. We paid £50 a night for a twin room, so £25 each per night is great value.
We found the staff very helpful and spoke good English. Pedry on reception was a credit to the hotel. The rooms are small and have no wardrobe but just 5 hangers. The shower was great. It had air conditioning and free wifi which worked a treat.
It was fairly easy to travel all over Paris from the hotel as it was a 3 minute walk from the Metro stations Crimee and Corentin Cariou on Line 7.
On arrival at Charles De Gaulle, it best to buy a train ticket for the week sold by Navigo. When you down the escalator to the ticket booths, then go to the rear of them to the ticket office and get a Navigo week pass there (€24 approx). You then have to put a photo on it , so take a passport pic with you to save you queuing up at the booth.
To get to the hotel:
Line B to Gare Du Nord,
Line 5 to Stalingrad,
Line 7 to Crimee or Corentin Cariou.

If you like good food in a Parisian bar then I recommend going down by the canal. The Bastringue on Quai de la Seine, was great for a drink and to eat and only 10 mins walk.

I fully recommend this hotel for the price we paid.

title: Decent Hotel but rooms are small
text:
I stayed here for 2 weeks on a business trip. I had to choose this location due to the proximity from my office. 

Location : Its is far from central Paris but metro station is just a couple of mins walk away. It also has a lot of small grocery stores (Franprix and Citymall) and eatery's nearby. (5/5)

Rooms : As highlighted by many reviewers, the rooms are really really small, its puny. I didnt even have enough space to open my luggage bag completely. On the other hand, they are clean and tidy with all basic amenities like Tea/Coffee maker and TV. Bathroom is also really tiny and only one person can fit in at a time. (3/5)

Staff : In general all staff members are friendly and nice. (5/5)

BUffet : Buffet has a decent spread nothing exceptional. (Croissants, scrambled eggs etc) (3/5)

Overall : It is decent hotel for people who are on a budget.But there are plenty of goot hotels in and around the area albeit for a slightly more price.

PS - The hotel provides free wifi which has decent speed.

title: Won’t revisit.
text:
The staff were friendly and the food in the bar delicious but some major problems at this hostel and will not be revisiting. We’ve stayed a dozens of hostels, a fair few St Christophers also. This one was far below standard. 

Cleanliness:
- Showers grotty. Walls weren’t wiped during out entire stay with mud streaks and hair stuck to them. 
- Signs everywhere advertising ‘cleaners on site 18 hours a day’ while it took them over 12 hours to mop up vomit in the hallway that has been reported numerous times. Even then, it wasn’t cleaned up properly. 

Communal Spaces:
- Access to the communal spaces was limited due to the chill out area being the home to over 10 trolleys of dirty bedding leaving slim room for guests. 
- The bar advertised as being included with the hostel was booked for private events during our stay limiting our ability to socialites, eat and drink within the hostel. This is one of the key features of a St Christopher’s and is advertised as a reason for booking. Not when it’s not available. 
- Communal bathrooms were subpar with soap dispensers empty, no hand dryers and hair dryers only available in the female toilets which is extremely sexist. 
- No where to fill up water bottles, no communal fountain or tap 
- We understand some hostels don’t provide kitchens due to having to maintain and clean them but the is often a fridge available to guests needing to store items. This was lacking. 

Breakfast:
- Not worth the paper it’s advertised on. 
- Watery coffee that never gets refilled. Stale week old bread buns and fruit that never gets replenished. Breakfast consisted of cornflakes and orange juice, we ended up just eating at local bakery’s. 
- No dairy milk alternatives for those that may be intolerant or vegan when the main elements of the lacking breakfast are dairy based.

title: A gem of a find in Paris
text: Being 40, I felt really old going to a hostel but the double I got on the 6th floor was great, with a fabulous balcony overlooking a kids playground and the canal close by. This is a very cute part of Paris and only ten minutes in a cab to Gare du Nord. The reason I’ve not given 5* is because the shower flooded the bathroom making it a bit of a slip risk but the front desk staff were brilliant and couldn’t do enough to help, even with the most basic of questions. Everyone I encountered working there was friendly, helpful and generous. Between that and a couple of great local restaurants close by this is a gem.

title: Good hostel for backpackers!!
text:

The room was spacious, bathrooms good and staff friendly, breakfast was okay and the food in the bar was lovely.

Main issue was the window was either fully open or not and as it was on a balcony on the Main Street we didn’t want to sleep with it open to the public so it was very hot! Also kind of annoying having people come in late/talk in the hall but I guess it comes with the territory.

title: A highschool hook up spot
text:

There is a bar underneath the rooms which is nice but the rooms were dirty, smelly, the windows were locked shut, and filled with high schoolers who were obviously just looking for a place to hookup. 

There are too many hostels in Europe to justify staying here.

title: Pleasant Hostel
text:

The lockers in our room were broken, would be nice if they were fixed.

title: attractive price-performance ratio
text:

They also offered a free walking tour, good wifi and reduced prices at the bar. The breakfast was modest, but they had cornflakes, and mini-baguettes so I was satisfied. The location is close to metro stations, but to walk it's a bit far from the city centre. However, I would recommend to stay there.

title: St Christopher Inn Canal, Paris
text:
I’ve stayed at St Christopher Inn Canal in Paris in August 2020. It’s not far from metro and and attractions are easily reached. Views of the Canal are beautiful and morning coffee at downstairs bar terrace is a pleasant start to a busy day.. My room was clean, had towels changed and bathroom cleaned daily. All the precautions for Covid-19 are implemented. Hand sanitation stations are plenty,. Wearing face mask in downstairs premises is compulsory: bar, reception, cleaning team and security are wearing face covering at all times. The crew is very friendly and helpful, will go an extra mile to make sure they deliver excellent service.
Now, the only drawback is that there’s no small fridge in private  en-suite rooms which is a complete disappointment. Usually August in Paris have a heat wave as this year too. The temperatures were reaching almost +40 C on the daily basis, the heat was unbearable . Of course there’s no air conditioning, after all it’s just a hostel. In such high temperatures not providing  this little luxury for private en-suite rooms is a big disappointment. If you’re looking for a longer stay ie. up to a week or over during hot, French summer and you don’t mind any of the above mentioned then that’s your place. If you’re looking for short stay in a clean, friendly place near shops  with great metro connections then this is a place for you too.
Btw my tv was broken, reception tried to fix it but sadly couldn’t. Would’ve been nice to watch a bit of news and metro at late night.
