We stayed at the hotel from 8/2-10 on the 29th floor. The room offers an excellent view of the city. Our room is with a view of The Eiffel Tower, the golden top of Invalides and Arc of Triumph. The room is spacious based on European standard. It is clean, modern, and comfortable. We were able to have our breakfast, buffet style, at the Club Lunge on the 34th floor, which offers a rich and tasty selections of food choices. We are a family of 3 generations and we all were able to find our favorite food there. The staff are friendly and responsive to take care our needs. When it was a bit crowded, they were able to expand the roof to find a table to accommodate our party of 6.  In addition to the breakfast,  the Club Lunge also offers snacks in the afternoon, which we also enjoyed very much. Paris is a great city to visit, but I will say that our stay at the Club Lunge is definitely one of the highlights of our trip. Since we stayed at the hotel for about a week and spent quite a few mornings and afternoons at the Lunge, we got to know the staff well. I would like to thank the supervisor, Slava, and his team, including Tenzin, Axelle, Raphael, and Falon, for their kind and warm service.

One comment about the hotel location. I was amazed that our hotel is only 3/4 mile away from the Arc of Triumph. And a Metro station for Line 1 is just around the corner of the hotel, which takes you directly to the old and elegant Les Marais district, and other parts of the city, but it involves to change to different Metro lines, which is just as complicated or as easy as any other metropolitan city. But the Paris Metro is clean and efficient.

title: we have stayed at this place for 6 times...
text:
We liked the location... it was easy to travel on trains [RER]...we walked all over the city to our favorite spots and ate at wide variety of places, near by.
room is small compared to American standard but was clean and would say 4+ ... room serivce was real nice ...they have a wonderful resturant and a small snacky place to buy... adjustant to the hotel is a big mall with a grocery store and bakery . we walk out  across the street and bought fresh baked stuff at local bakery.   and we enjoyed couple times view of Eiffel tower from our window.... couple times other famous spots... I love Paris and really do not have anything bad to say about this area or experiences. Best was walking around to all famous places... eating local food and going to few famous eating places... people were friendly ....Hyatt is a great place to be.

title: A View to Remember
text:
With one of the best views of Paris, this is easily one of the best hotels. 
Of course, there are different views, and not all rooms face the Eiffel Tower. 

Still, very comfortable and very close to a metro station.

title: Nice hotel, OK location
text: The hotel is recently renovated and very up to date. My only complaint about the rooms was the lack of top sheet on the bed. It was way too hot for a heavy duvet,  but that seems to the style in Europe. You have the option of sleeping without a cover or sweating all night. The view from the room was incredible, but the location was just ok. A lot of construction around the hotel and many restaurants nearby were closed. The metro was close and easy to use. If I ever return to Paris and circumstances allowed I would spend the extra money to be closer to the center, but this hotel is an excellent option if you are on a tighter budget.

title: Hyatt Regency Paris Etoile
text: Very convenient to Meeting and Conference Spaces.  Lots of small local restaurants within walking distance.  Good views from upper rooms.. Staff very cordial. Hard to get Ubers but lots of Taxis available.

title: Nice hotel friendly to foreigners
text: Our trip to Paris was for a convention next door, which made the Hyatt a great location.  The staff were very friendly and helpful, speaking English without the need to explain country of origin.  Breakfast spread was generous and easily accessed.

title: Cleanliness
text: We had a great stay but the room cleanliness was below standard. Needs to be improved, carpet was not hoovered at all and bedsheets were stained, we asked them to change it and they did so. Staff were helpful

title: Beautiful Hotel
text: The Hyatt Regency Etoile is a very nice hotel and exceeded our expectations.  Our rooms were nicely appointed and had spectacular views of the city.  The Regency Club room was well stocked with good wine and the attendants were extremely professional.  I would definitely stay there again and would recommend it to my family and friends.

title: The Hyatt Etoile
text: Beautiful hotel with stunning views of Paris. Very convenient location to the sites. Fantastic staff. Overall a great hotel. The sky bar was a lovely place to end out evenings and our children were welcome.

title: Best place to stay in Paris
text: Stay here for the staff.  Exceptional front desk staff who were fluent in multiple languages and go out of there way to ensure you have a smooth check in process.  We upgraded to the Executive Suite, which had 2 large rooms and lots of space.  Breakfast was also outstanding, whether in the downstairs restaurant or at the Regency Club. Service was amazing at both places and the view from the 34th floor was fabulous. Great location near the #1 Metro line.  Just walk through the mall for the shortest and coolest path.  Money change in the adjacent mall with great rates. Would definitely stay here in the future.  The kids did not want to leave.

title: Great Hotel
text: The Hyatt Regency Paris Etoile is a terrific place to stay.  The staff is terrific, courteous and very helpful.  There are always taxi's to take you wherever you wish to go.  The rooms are clean and the beds are very comfortable.

title: Did not willingly provide Globalist benefits until pushed
text: This is a nice hotel brought down by the employees including night management.  As a Globalist, I was entitled to a suite upgrade based on availability which I verified before checking in around 1 am.  However, the front desk person who barely spoke English and didn't answer my basic question did not provide us with a suite even though he told us that we were getting a suite.  Then, after contacting the night manager Sara regarding this issue, she lied and stated that all standard suites were sold out (they were not, I'm a seasoned traveler and I verified availability).  When I pushed her on this issue after she put us in an upgraded room (but not a suite), she lied again and said that "there was a cancellation" (at 1:15 am?!?) and suddenly we got our suite.  Being lied to was completely unnecessary and left a terrible taste in my mouth.  How about this - simply honor the stated benefits and then you don't have to embarrass yourself when you get called out on your lies?

title: Spectacular View of Eiffel Tower
text: Hotel is well-connected to public transport amenities and offers spectacular view of Eiffel Tower from its king deluxe room. Great customer service and breakfast experience. Would highly recommend it to anyone coming to Paris.

title: Good for a short trip
text: We had points and stayed for free with lounge access. The rooms are small but we weren’t in the room except to sleep. There is construction going on around the hotel, which didn’t bother us (we couldn’t hear it on the 32nd floor), but didn’t make for very picturesque walks to/from the metro. Although not located right in the middle of the tourist areas, it was easy to take the metro everywhere.  The lounge had a great breakfast and happy hour. Beautiful view of the Eiffel Tower!

title: Extraordinary
text:
I didn't expect this level of service after COVID. It was a nice surprise to me. The personal is always taking care of your needs. The food is good. 
The Mayo market is a great idea for a quick fix in the late hours.

title: Excellent
text: I was there for work, everything was exceptionally Fast at check-in, Very professional, Friendly and very Courteous. The Manager Hugo ( Boss ) at the front office is excellent and very hard working. The next day at Break fast every  one  was helpful, How ever Jade in my section was amazing, Courteous, professional and very attentive. Room was Not renovated one, still did the job and was clean.

title: Extremely disappointed at the level of customer service and quite astonishing for a Hyatt hotel
text:
We were in Paris two weeks ago for our honeymoon which we kicked off with Fete Nationale (Bastille Day). I reached out to Windo Sky Bar, about 1 month prior, to make reservations for the “Sparkling Night with a View” event being held the night of July 14th. I exchanged half a dozen emails with Ms. Eva Merian who stated that we could not make a reservation but the space would be open on a first come first served basis. We adjusted our plans accordingly and shortly after arriving in Paris, we made our way to Windo Sky Bar to prepare for the evening. We arrived around 7PM to a completely empty space and were greeted by a manager who told us that we could not be seated for the night. I explained the numerous emails with his staff in which he stated that he made a “last minute change”. 

A note to management. DO NOT offer the option of “first come first served” if it is not truly available. I would’ve preferred if someone said that the space was reservation only so I could continue to look for options that would be better suited for myself and my husband. And at the very least, they could have allowed us to enjoy the space for a short time before releasing our table to those with reservations. No accommodations were made.

To say we were disappointed is an understatement.

title: New hotel experience
text: First time we visit this hotel in the park 17 arrondissement and is a bit of a drive to the opera house or the Louvre. The rooms were great and good size too. The hotel doesn’t have parking facilities  but there’s one a block away Indigo Etoile Meridien for around € 39 a night.

title: Amazing Experience
text: This is the most amazing stay I have ever had at any Hotel. They did all the efforts to satisfy our needs and they managed to give us a great room facing Eifel tower and managed to provide consultation for us on how to spend an unplanned vacarion.

title: The most amazing view of Paris
text:
It was my first time in Paris and I asked for a room in a high floor. The front desk person assigned me a room on the 32nd floor. It was a derream come true. Unforgettable. I enjoyed the most incredible views of Paris day and night and made lots of pictures and videos. 
The viw from the bar is also incredible as well as the cocktails and food, not to talk about the kindness of the staff. 
Breakfast is excellent, with marvelous french vienoisserie, cheeses (I'm a fan!!), seasonal fruits... mmmmm. I hope I'll come back some day with my husband!
The location is incredible also not only because of the views but also because you will be walking distance form some of the most beautidfuful spots of Paris, and just a few meters from the mestro or train stating to go anywhere in Paris in minutes!
One reccommendation: plan your movements walking or in metro, traffic can bre tricky in the area!!

title: Wonderful Paris Hotel
text: Despite the 104 degree heat, the hotel was so comfortable. The staff, rooms and restaurant were all excellent…especially the breakfast buffets. The location wasn’t near Paris attractions and we needed cabs. But the neighborhood has many wonderful cafes.

title: Nice Hyatt
text: This is close to restaurants and metro- - Breakfast is good very large selection was very good.  the view at the top of the hotel is a great view of the city, but the folks at the top of the building have some attitude.  In Paris, I would stay there again.  The front desk was very warm and helpful

title: Delighful hotel and stay
text:
Beautiful hotel and great service! Definitely worth the extra money or points for club amenities. The only downside was there was construction outside in both the front and back which created confusion for our taxi driver when arriving and leaving, and also for getting to and from the subway (located through a connected mall at the rear of the hotel).  

For what its worth, the shower was amazing, as were the quality of the linens and towels.

Unfortunately, the 34th floor Windo SkyBar was closed for renovation and I had been looking forward to seeing the view and having a meal and drinks there. The 34th floor Regency Club was also closed, but was relocated to the main level and still offered breakfast and snacks and beverages. During the current heatwave being able to stay in the hotel to relax and have a glass of wine was definitely welcome! 

I'm not planning on heading back to Paris anytime soon, but will definitely stay at this Hyatt again, if I do!

title: horrible service ,not 4 star
text: The staff with a black face all the way ,and very rude,looks like I own them. No politely greeting! No smile!!! No helpful! Bathroom not very clean with used lotion and shower gel.Water is so cold which my colleagues complained as well. Noisy from the metal pipe , I have no idea what's that. The traffic in front of the hotel is horrible. Every time when you out ,you have to wasted at least 30-40 minutes to wait for the taxi at the entrance. The service even worse than the UK 2 star hotels. Don't recommend !

title: Excellent location, Staff are very friendly and helpful, room view is excellent.
text:
Excellent location, safe, clean ，close to  
everywhere. Staffs are very friendly and helpful. Room view is excellent, enjoy the club lounge. Close to subway, easily explore the city. Nice choice when stay at Paris!

title: Poor checkin experience
text: Very poor front desk staff knowledge and  professionalism. After more than 12 hrs long trip and despite my 2 months before hand request early checkin, my children ended sleeping on chairs in the lobby and checkin close to 4 pm instead. The rooms were not ready and we were given different rooms. Front desk ladies didn’t show any understanding or sympathy, so what! One of them told me when I was expressing my frustration!! Never going to that hotel again. It could have been an isolated incident but it was the worst checkin ever.

title: Excellent
text:
Great property with excellent views of the city and very helpful staff specially the Concierge team. Location is great for connectivity to different parts of the city through public transport.
One area for improvement would be the options on the food menu (dining and breakfast) - there is scope to add more variety specially for vegetarian options

title: Near the Arc de T and the Champ de L'
text:
Great Hotel, good location.  Clean room and quality finishings.  Well maintained hotel.
Early check-in was the only down side.  They offer it on the web, yet in person its a NO. That is unacceptable.  Then when they take your number and promise to call you when its done being cleaned then don't call you

title: Highly Recommend the Hyatt Etoile
text: Every aspect of our stay at the Hyatt Etoile met our expectations.  The WINDO restaurant on the 34th floor was a wonderful addition and our room was comfortable, clean and offered an incredible view of the city.  The MAYO market offered a wide array of foods and drinks, including bottles of champagne, wine and waters.  There were delicious meals that were healthy and representative of the local foods. The staff was incredible and met our every need.

title: Best avoided with so much construction
text: Stayed for four nights with a Viking cruise... very modern hotel with amenities.  However, we were assigned a "handicapped accessible" room which was very uncomfortable, and had a roll in shower with curtain.  The hotel was packed and we had a view of the Eiffel Tower, so we did not ask to be moved.  The location is far from the must see sites, and there is construction surrounding the hotel which makes it dangerous to navigate for pedestrians.

title: Not a 4stars service
text: To begin with, it is the first time that I get to a hotel and I have to queue for check-in. I had paid more to have a room on the high floor with a view to the Eiffel Tower and they gave me the middle floor, and when I complained they told me that from the 8th floor it is considered high (of a tower of 30 floors). You have to pay extra for breakfast in the room. When I went down for breakfast my name didn't come out so I had to wait  again and fix it. And with the check-out I had to wait one more time and go from counter to counter because the system was not working and then the printer was not working to print an invoice that I did not ask them to print. The service is diplomatic but does not help or solve anything.  There is no place where you can work from, yes in 4 star hotel with 30 floors. definitely a bad experience. The stars go to the view from the room.

title: Decent Location; less than decent everything else
text:
Short and sweet - I've stayed here twice and had bad experiences both times. I won't stay here again and encourage most people reading to find other accommodations. 

The location isn't horrible - next to a mall and a short walk to many restaurants. And you'll have to go offsite for food and drink since they won't actually serve you on site. At least, that was my experience the one time this trip I tried. 

I won't drop her name here, since this review is (honest and fair, yet) negative, but the person that tried to help me check in at first was as helpful as she could have been. Of course, the system wasn't taking payments for some reason, the Hyatt app showed I'd be upgraded to a room that wasn't available, and I was checked into a room that was dirty (wet towel on the bathroom floor) with "no alternative room" available. Forgot the room, I should have insisted they check me into another hotel. 

In the future, I'll save them the trouble. I won't be back and I highly encourage you all to look elsewhere.

title: Bad attitude of manager
text:
Just stay here for one night to see the fireworks on 14 July. I understand today must be very busy but the way that person did was not acceptable.
So we arrived at the lobby there was no guests in the line, there were two counters no guests and we were just wondering if we should go directly or just wait in the line. Then this person from the lobby yelled in the lobby said “please line up there”. He said please but the tone was so bad and rude which I didn’t expect it at all. I’m sure he is the manager because staff went to him to solve the problem. And when he yelled no one dared to say anything, there is no way anyone can be this rude. Well I didn’t say anything since I know he is the manager but I wonder if he can treat guests like this how does he treat the staff. 
The girl who checked in was friendly, the touch screen for the screen doesn’t work very well and I tried 2 different panels to get to the floor I want to go.

title: Excellent  value for money
text: Excellent location easily accesible on foot and via metro from most major Paris sites,  no fuss but modern areas and rooms, clean, excellent breakfast, stunning views of eiffel tower from the higher level rooms, professional and friendly staff - all  aforementioned at a very reasonable price considering Paris hotel prices. I am a regular visitor in Paris and throughout the years I have stayed in much more luxurious hotels ( and much more expensive) and I consider this Hyatt one the best value for money hotels, considering all parameters. I would like to make a special mention to the very capable concierge team  and in particular to  Olivier head of concierge, Max and Djamell head iof security who really went out of their way to assit me in finding a mobile phone that was forgotten in a taxi. They are an asset to the hotel and I am extremely grateful.

title: Hotel BREACH reservation contract (swap from booked expensive Tower SUITE to cheaper ROOM)
text:
I am Hyatt globalist.
Please allow me share my worst stay at Hyatt Regency Paris Etoile.
Even now, I still feel very painful at the moment I wrote.

My family had Europe travel plan. Feb 28, I booked and paid 24k points "Eiffel tower SUITE" check-in May 21 2022, one night,  for 3 adults. Hyatt emailed confirmation Reservation number 35313026
Room Type: EIFFEL TWR STE, Room Description:.. living room:
2 bathrooms: walk-in.

After check-in 7+pm May 21, We got the room key, entered room,
dropped luggage into room, grabbed some snack from club,
hurry up city tour excitedly.

At midnight, we came back, after 5 hours city tour,  we were so tired,
just wanted to take showers and sleep. But we can not find 2nd bathroom, living room( with Murphy bed), We just realized we did not get the Tower SUITE as we booked and paid. It is  Eiffel ROOM only.

Around 00:30 am, I  went down to the lobby, there was only one check-in staff, 5 more guests lined up to check-in, no other staffs at sight. I waited in line 30+ minutes. When I got my turn, I politely told check-in desk staff Tsering, I am Hyatt globalist. I booked Suite and paid, but I only get Tower ROOM. Is there any other connecting room to my current room ?

Check-in staff Tsering, he checked my reservation record and check my key.  He said there were two type of Suites in this building. The room I got now is right for my reservation, no 2nd bathroom, no living room. I told him that email confirmation shows the suite has living room and two bathrooms. Why you told me that I don't
have living room and second bathroom. He denied everything and refused to give me Suite as I booked and paid.

This is legal contract issue. H.R. Paris Etoile breached our contract.
(Guest booked Tower SUITE, but Hotel swapped to Tower ROOM after check-in).

Even elementary school student can tell the difference between "two bathroom" and "one bathroom".  How can hotel staff Tsering don't know it ?

My families and me were so shocked and we don't have two beds to sleep. We went to lobby again and awaited concierge desk staff that we need help from manager.  A female manager showed up. She confirmed we should have connected room which has murphy bed, living room, and second bathroom.
So she make new room key to open door to connected room.  It already passed 1:30am now, I lost  all sleep mood. My hart filled with exhausted after fight hard to right suite back. My two families lost sleep either.

The two check-in desk staffs should know there is connected room for Tower SUITE.
Why both staffs refused to give me connected room and insist that my booking has only one bed, one bathroom, and no living room.

Next day, May 22 noon, I received email form VP stating she compensated 5,000 points for our inconvenience. Hotel manager also emailed me sorry later
days after I gave 0 star feedback.

VP manager compensated 5k points  is far less than the the pain we suffered !

It is not just inconvenience! It's pain. It's legal issue!

Check-in staff should never swap expensive Tower SUITE to cheaper Tower ROOM, and lied to us that's our booking.

title: Best place to live and enjoy stunning view of eiffel tower in Paris
text: It is only sky scrapper hotel in Paris and eiffel tower view from the room is quite exciting and makes your stay perfect in this beautiful hotel....Breakfast is good with many options for vegetarians also,bit it could be more customized with some live counters....staff is very good and always you will get taxi on the gate to travel anywhere in the city...best thing for an Indian is the Water jet in the washroom, which makes our stay more comfortable and which reflects this hotel as true international brand.Luggage storage facility also makes it a quite easy deal to visit france and nearby countries without carrying much luggage. Real feel of Hyatt brand in Paris...near to all main attractions and easy connectivity with Metro, RRTS, bus and all modes of public transport...

title: Great view, a bit weird food
text: This is probably one of the best views hotel in the city, but food and breakfast are a bit strange: small oval plates, which is very inconvenient for eating, little selection, not good coffee. Design of the hotel and cleanness is very nice.

title: If you need to stay in the area, this is a good option
text: If you need to be near the periphery of Paris, this is a good choice. Lovely breakfast buffet as well as lunch. Beautiful view from 34th floor. Not good for general Paris visits (too far from most sites) but otherwise solid.

title: Modern Hotel with access to Metro 1
text: While there was a lot of construction surrounding the hotel, noise levels were normal for an urban site. Very clean, staff pleasant, and I felt welcomed. Our room was well laid out. Like the automatic lights that illuminated the floor when leaving the bed in the dark. Shower controller easy to understand and use. The takeout food unit was well stocked and enjoyed the variety of salads offered. The recommended restaurants all were excellent. I felt safe in the neighborhood. The subway was close and we used it daily to get to the center of Paris.

title: Worst hotel I have ever stayed in in europe.
text: The room was small toilet was up against the wall. No shelves to put anything down . No real shower. More like we were camping.  The bathroom flooded because blocked drain. No face cloths ,TV would not stay on. No couch leaving only room to hold 1 suitcase. Coffee in room was missing 1st morning. Tried it on second morning undrinkable.. Coffee at morning buffet was good once you could get it. Always 1 or more of the machines inoperable, causing long lines. Food was good with very good variety. Worst hotel I have ever stayed in ,in all of Europe. We have visited 12 times in the last 15 years. Staff was cordial. Probably could have used a couple more during breakfast buffet, however this is happening all over and is to be expected.  We would never stay in this hotel again

title: Amazing staff, top of line services, great rooms, and good location.
text: This was our honeymoon and also birthday trip for my husband. This Hyatt provided us services better than many Andaz and on par of Park Hyatt we have been to. The Globalist VIP Manager Renetta, and Club Lounge Manager Letisha, were just exceptional. The rooms are new and well maintained. We had the best view of the Eiffel Tower directly from our room window! There is a full gym, and a few restaurants. The Club on site also offer the BEST breakfast we have ever seen, with full protein selections, eggs, vegetables, fruit, full bakery, coffee & tea & juices, the list just goes on. This is not typical of European hotels to offer such an extensive breakfast option. The hotel is directly attached to a shopping mall, movie/concert theater, restaurants, and a large Metro and RER train station. It is only about 0.8 miles and a 15 min walk to the Arc de Triomphe. There is also a Photomaton right in the mall, which makes taking and printing selfies for passports and Navigo cards extremely convenient (you will need to provide the ticket agents a physical print out of a passport size selfie to purchase and activate the Navigo cards, or you can get fined if caught). The Metro ride into the center of the city by the Louvre, Palais Garnier, Pompidou is only about 20 min from the hotel. Since the RER train is directly at the hotel, you can also easily access Chateau Versailles, and even Mont Saint-Michel in Normandy, making the 2 visits above as day trips. Rooms are quiet, clean, and modern. I cannot highly recommend this place. We will go back over and over again.

title: Speechless
text: There are few hotels that leave me speechless. Hyatt Regency Paris Etoile is among them. The best of the best staff, kind, helpful, hard working, friendly. Appreciated those who checked us in, and when one of our rooms wasn’t ready, they let us wait in the club lounge, and delivered the keys there when ready. Club lounge staff were really on top of things. Very attentive and kept everything well stocked and clean. Mayo restaurant staff were similarly wonderful. Food was stocked as soon as it ran low. Housekeeping also really wonderful, with limited ability to communicate, was patient with me to figure out that one night, we just needed extra conditioner, nothing else. Last but not least, the team that helped with setting up a small surprise for the very special occasion we were celebrating outdid themselves! I can’t wait to return to Paris and stay here!

title: Best stay at Hyatt in a *long* time
text:
Great staff, great location, good enough quality food/beverages at Hyatt Lounge, great views ... 34th floor WINDO provided outstanding service and views o Eiffel Tower at night, etc.

We stayed using Hyatt Visa card freebie nights and are no longer BLUE/BLACK level  with Hyatt (but TITANIUM ELITE for Life at Marriott, etc. etc.) ... still great treatment (we did not get view of Eiffel Tower from our rooms, but our 2 rooms were free) .. rather than eat high priced hotel food, our teens and I headed out late one night to the 4-5 kebab/cous cous/hamburger joints next to Pharmacie across the street ... great French fast food, great prices ... concierge team was great reminding us of certain METRO (subway) strategies ... and Gautier (sp?) at front door/car man was great in helping us navigate into front area of hotel to drop off our luggage before heading to the INDIGO (Le Meridien) public parking

title: An excellent view on Paris. Hotel worth to choose because of window view.
text: No water at the reception desk during check in time. Only one small shampoo and one small body gel for two people in the room to share. Small rooms. Huge problems with getting the invoice for the stay in the hotel. Hotel worth to stay because of an excellent view on Paris. Because of the view my favorite choice in Paris.

title: Lovely hotel - excellent front of house staff
text:
Fantastic hotel....staff were excellent. Breakfast was amazing - covered all options and extremely well presented.
Front of house staff and breakfast staff were very engaging and couldn't do enough for you.
Highly recommended

title: Paris July 2023
text: Great hotel, staff very pleasant and helpful. Food great and very clean. Must say a visit to the Skybar at night is a must, views of the Eiffel Tower are breath taking, however tye bar is very expensive.

title: Wonderful Modern Hotel with Excellent Service
text:
I am staying at the Hyatt Regency Paris Etoile for business and I have to say, I am so pleased with my stay.  The hotel is clean, modern, sophisticated and is an excellent central location.  My room has the BEST view of the Eiffel Tower!  The fitness center is perfect for my needs and the food at Mayo downstairs is fresh and delicious.

One highlight of my trip has been the Windo Skybar where you can relax and watch the Eiffel tower light up at night.  I must give very high praise to Eva Merian who is the head of Corporate Leadership Training F&B for the Hyatt Regency Paris Etoile.  She has been incredibly gracious, professional, warm and watching her in action at Windo with clientele and her staff is impressive.  She was juggling a large crowd last night and she did it effortlessly and with true grace.  The Hyatt Regency Paris Etoile is very lucky to have her and she has already made my stay here so pleasant!  Thank you Eva!

Thank you Hyatt Regency Paris Etoile!

title: Loved it!
text:
Zero regrets staying there!
It's spotless, beautiful and the staff was very helpful.  We upgraded to an Eiffel Tower view room on a higher floor and the view was gorgeous!
The beds were comfy, and the bathroom was modern and beautiful.

The only thing that could have made it better would be a guest self-service laundry.  Otherwise it really made our Paris visit perfect!  

Highly recommend!

title: Busy, not relaxing
text:
The first obstacle was getting on the elevator.  Many people checking in at the same. time and the elevator system required you to enter your floor at which point the "smart. system" would advise you which elevator to take. However, the assigned elevators did not seem to appear as the system indicated they would and you had to fight through a crowd to get to one. The room itself was fine, but had no soap, shampoo or conditioner in the bathroom.  A call to the desk resulted in shower gel only being delivered.  The next day housekeeping provided a complete array of products.

The hotel was very busy with various groups and airline crews.  The buffet breakfast was quite good.  Several good restaurants were in walking distance.  Construction of a new metro station created a traffic jam around the hotel at all times and  made walking to nearby restaurants more difficult.

At checkout, the concierge was not able to get a. van taxi for our party of 4 and then provided absolutely no help in getting a regular cab.  As we tried to get one on our own, we discovered the construction allowed very limited access to the front of the hotel and was made even worse by the display of 6-8 very upscale cars parked in front of the hotel for some type of event.  As if that was not enough, some of the cars were started and revved up which made an unbelievable amount of noise including backfires which sounded like gun shots.  I finally walked out in the stalled traffic to get a cab which was available. 

I would stay there again only as a last resort.

title: Huge hotel that connects to a mall
text: Clean rooms with great views of Eiffel Tower. Great check-in with Tsering at the front desk. Rooms were a bit small, but we had connecting rooms for our family of 4 so at least we had two bathrooms. Great breakfast if you are a club member-snacks and drinks also offered in club later in the day

title: Great stay
text:
This hotel has great service, from the sparkling live hotel lobby to the quiet room and the amazing vieuw in the club area staff did everything to make your stay enjoyable. The beds are very good and the rooms have a decent size.
Cleanlyness all over.

title: Paris Etoile

title: Overall pretense of this hotel is completely unsatisfying and even annoying.
text:
Hotel de Neuville, 17e Paris
While this hotel has a homely feeling it is a deception in several ways. There are many things wrong with this hotel, and just a few things they got right. It is definitely no four-star hotel, but that erroneous rating might be more the fault of Paris tourist officials.
First, note that the hotel is not really very close to the Arc de Triomphe, which is more than thirty minutes away walking. 
Its management seems unorganized. This probably accounts for why it always appears to be understaffed or staffed with untrained employees. As a result it offers guests few services. There is no doorman, no concierge, no reservation office, no newspapers, no information about Paris, no shop, it provides no accessories like a toothbrush if you forgot. It is a very basic hotel.
The hotel cancelled our reservation, not once but twice and still charged us. The first reservation was made by telephone directly with the hotel. When this was cancelled we made it again online at their website. They charged my credit card and we had a confirmation email from them, but when we arrived they did not have the reservation. They apparently cancelled it without telling us. After about thirty minutes of wrangling we sorted it out, but they falsely claimed they didn’t charge me for the online reservation. They did according to my bank statement and I had to convince my bank to reverse the charge. The hotel demanded payment a second time.
The rooms are tiny and claustrophobic. The room key didn’t work repeatedly. Two people will constantly bump into each other in the room.  The double rooms are really single rooms, which can’t comfortably fit anything bigger than a single bed. They were inexcusably cluttered with furniture that does not really seem to have much of a purpose. There was a commercial quality Nespresso in the room and a tea kettle hidden in the closet. The closet space is acceptable for a two-day trip. There was also a safe in the closet, but no iron. 
The toilet and bathroom are separate. The toilet is terrible; it is in a small closet and virtually unusable.  You can not sit on it naturally, but have to sit titled to your right on the loo if you are over 4 feet tall. The bathroom has a towel warmer, which is a plus. There is also a terrace connected to the bathroom, but it doesn’t look like it will support a person standing on it. The bathroom is so small that you almost step out of the window getting out of the tub-shower. There is only one body-hair wash and when I used it on my hair it left it very dry. When I read the ingredients, they read more like an industrial clearer than a wash for humans. Always look under the sink as that is where they hide the tissues and the hair dryer as there is no space for then anywhere else. The towels were good quality, but everyday brought in different qualities.
There is an elevator, but it is too small to hold two people and a suitcase. The stairs are steep and one flight will likely wear out anyone over fifty who is not in the best of fitness.  There’s no gym, no pool, a very small café, which is also the lobby, bar, breakfast room, and reception area. 
The breakfast is sparse. There are three cereals, some nuts and dried fruits, assorted breads, eggs you can boil, non-descript sausages, and a small serving of scrambled eggs for the guest that gets it first. An overwhelmed, but kind woman can bring you the coffee of your choice or water for the assorted tea bags that were available. The mini croissants and mini pains au chocolat are the usual top Parisian quality. The assortment of condiments include not only jams, but also include somewhat confusingly mayonnaise and ketchup. The breakfast did not change in three days.
There are no newspapers or magazines available, although they advertise on materials in the room that they are available. There is actually almost no material in the multipurpose lobby. There is natural and carbonated water from a faucet. This hotel used to be a Best Western, it’s not clear if it still is, but it is unlikely it would make that chain’s grade.
There was no view from our room, except I to the back of other buildings. This view is not so unusual in Paris, so can’t really fault the hotel. Nevertheless, for a superior room in a four-star hotel the view was as poor quality as it gets.
The cleaning and hygiene appears to leave much to desired. There was an article left behind by a guest or the cleaning staff on the chair in our room. The toilet paper roll was well used and carpet looked half cleaned. The sheets and bed seemed okay, but the red pillows needed cleaning. Going up the stairs I heard guests were coughing excessively. The kind and hard-working cleaning woman wore neither a mask nor gloves. During our stay I wore a mask as much as possible as there is still an ongoing pandemic in France as of June 2022. No hotel staff took any precautions that were noticeable.
The reception is as small and as cluttered as the rooms. The receptionists even more scattered. One seemed completely overwhelmed by the mess the hotel had made of our reservation. On top of it she was rude, warning me that she would need payment in advance as if their mistake was my fault. She did eventually apologize blaming the mistake on another colleague who was new. Really very unprofessional. Another receptionist seemed just dumbfounded merely repeating I hope you enjoyed your stay to anything said to her. And a third was kind, it seemed to disappear for up to thirty minutes at time. The hotel appears to be run by amateurs. They were friendly and generally polite.
The hotel does have a home-like feeling, but that is the best that can be said. Business professionals will likely not appreciate the chaos, holiday-makers will likely seek something more comfortable.
This is not a four-star hotel and should not be charging it’s four-star prices that run in excess of two hundred Euros a night. It is at best an average three-star hotel. Anyone paying over €120 ($130) a night to stay here is getting ripped off. The overall pretense of this hotel is completely unsatisfying and even annoying.

I had a bad experience here though due to some idiot banging consistently on another guests door in the middle of the night - but that isn’t their fault.

However,  what really put me off returning was when I came down for breakfast the attitude of the person supposedly looking after the breakfast area. 

If you are not going to leave coffee out, the least you can do is offer guest one - I watched as various people came down - looked around quizzically - and either went without coffee or eventually asked around - the person concerned hardly deigned to come into the breakfast area

That said, the other front desk staff were so helpful I still give this 4. Until breakfast it would have become a regular stay for me - maybe I just got them at the wrong time

title: Extremely clean and quiet hotel in a nice area of Paris
text: If your priority is cleanliness and ease of getting around either on foot or via metro or bus then this hotel is ideal. Situated in the 17eme, its location is in a quiet, leafy suburb of Paris within walking distance of the Arc de Triomphe (not a short walk I hasten to add so if walking is not your thing, take the No. 31 bus). If you opt to walk, Boulevard Pereire will eventually lead you directly onto the Avenue De La Grande Armee at the end of which is the Arc de Triomphe. If you fancy taking a brief detour, just off the top of Boulevard Pereire is le Palais des Congrès de Paris which is a great place to stop for a bite to eat, visit designer boutiques and fill up on current cultural events.

title: Paris under the Arc
text: We chose the Best Western Hotel Plus de Neuville Arc de Triomphe to meet up after a 19 year hiatus.  It was a lovely boutique hotel, in a beautiful old 19 century mansion house which is just a stones throw away from the Arc de Triomphe.   The hotel still retaines all of its wonderful old world charms, winding staircases opulent velvet seating in a warm contemporary colored palette.  There is a great choice of a continental breakfast from croissants to scrambled eggs to start off your day.  There are also a number of good cafes and restaurants nearby and the nearest Metro and RER station is Pereire Levallois just a few hundred yards from the hotel itself.  The location was fantastic for us and the breakfast and lounge area was just perfect to stop and relax after a long day out and about in Paris. I would strongly recommend this hotel as it is also incredibly clean and modern and made for a comfortable and much appreciated stay.

title: Hospitality missing
text:
Best Western in France is usually nice so I booked this hotel because of its proximity to my conference.  I arrived after a grueling 5 hours of traveling, the last hour on my feet, carrying luggage in crowded metros at rush hour.  I was exhausted and dying to put my bags down and put my feet up.
Unfortunately, I arrived at 8pm, which was the changing of the guards at the front desk.  The check in guy asked for my name and saw that my room was prepaid and only for 1 night.  instead of spending 15 seconds and just handing me my key, he asked me to wait while he transferred all his shift information to the night guy. I was made to feel like I came at an inconvenient time and should wait until they are good and ready for me. They spent the next 5 minutes talking about minute details and stacks of paper and finally the night shift guy put on his name tag, asked me for my name and gave me a key.  VERY FRUSTRATING!!!  When will the French learn that when you work in the hospitality industry, the guests are the priority and not an inconvenience. 
The room was very nicely decorated and spacious by French standards.  The bathroom was clean and well appointed, big fluffy towels which I love.  I had windows that open for fresh air.  The bed was comfortable and the sheets very luxurious.
Such a shame the check in was such a bad experience.

title: Quiet and Quirky
text:
Lovely little hotel in a quiet area. If walking from Pereire Lavallois station you just need to come out front of station at Marechal Juin exit and turn immediately right! Blvd Periere has 2 sides- south and north! You need north- road with Flocco restaurant at bottom! We went wrong way and it took us a while to find it!

Room was clean, had all we needed, and comfortable. Hotel lift must hold the record for the smallest ever- not even the size of our shower tray at home!! But we fitted in ok with our little cases!!

All the staff we came across were kind and helpful. We didn’t have breakfast so can’t comment. Restaurant on the square called Royal Periere does breakfast for 5 euros so we went there!

Hope the following helps-

If you are flying in/ out of CDG airport- take RER B to St Michel Notre Dame, then change to RER C to Periere Lavallois! See above for directions to hotel! Do same in reverse when going back to airport, allow about 2 hours each way as could easily take this long to get across Paris! 

Everything was close by via metro/ train. Best way to see Paris? 

For us was by train/on foot/river boat.

 Batobus on Seine - such good value for money - hop on hop off boat to all the sites, no commentary but who needs it when you have Google? We spent 5 hours going from one place to another! 17 euros each!

Can recommend Chez Gustave and Castell Cafe near Eiffel Tower! Pizza Pino on Champs Elysses ( did 2 courses for 13 euros!) 

Merci

title: Excellent service and an impeccably capable manager!
text: My wife and I chose this hotel as our base in Paris, as we celebrated our anniversary. Right from the get go, it was obvious that the staff places a high priority on service. We arrived earlier than the 2 pm check-in time, but they tried their best to turn the room around so that we would not have to wait long. The lobby has a small, pleasing lounge area where we cooled our heels while the room was getting readied. It also has a cute bar which is great for a beverage or two. Mr. Roland Wang, the manager, deserves a special mention. He upgraded us to a Superior room when he found out that we were celebrating our anniversary, and the gesture was much appreciated! Beyond that, he was genuinely warm and affable. We saw him running around, taking care of sundry things,  on various days - it is obvious he takes deliberate pride in running the establishment. Kudos to him and his staff! The rooms are small, but that is the norm for Paris, and all in all, we were more than comfortable. I suspect that the Superior rooms are a bit more spacious than the standard ones. The bathrooms were very well appointed. The neighborhood is very residential, and we found that to be a refreshing change of pace after the hustle and bustle of downtown Paris. It is a nice neighborhood and we had fun exploring some restaurants and patisseries in the vicinity. We felt like locals! The proximity to the metro and the RER C line is a huge plus, and even though you are 25 minutes from the Parisian attractions, it is very easy to get there via the metro/RER. Thanks, Roland! We hope to see you again in the near future!

text:
Buddy and I booked this place the night before we planned to stay there, we chose the two twin option.  Upon arriving, clerk confirmed the two twins and sent us to the room.  Surprise, only one bed.  I went down to talk to clerk, and he informed me that was the only room left (seemed odd since he told me it was two t\wins before I even asked about. it).  So we did not start off on the right foot.

The room itself was small, but very tastefully done.  Toilet was separate from the bathroom which was helpful in this small of the room.  This was one of the few rooms during our 3 week trip that allowed us to get the AC to a comfortable temperature.  

Location- a bit detached separated from the main parts of tourist Paris.  However, it did allow for a 20 minute walk to the Arc De Triumph that was pretty much a straight shot, which also put you on the Champ DeElysses.  There were some nice cafes right around the corner as well.

The elevator was extremely small.  I fit in it with one bag on the way up, but I swore not to take it again.  It was small and hot, I just used it to take my bag down as I walked down the steps the next morning.

I arranged with the staff to arrange a car for the airport the next day.  The car was late, supposedly help up by traffic (when isn't there traffic there).  Hotel then arranged another car for me, which arrived about 40 minutes after the scheduled time.  I have no idea how the hotel/car service relationship works, but if hotel gets some sort of payment for arranging the service, they really need to choose better.

All of that being said, I recommend the room, but when you arrange for twin beds, and the site lets you book them, that type of room should be available, and if it isn't, the hotel should comp. you free breakfast, or some other type of amenity,

title: A welcoming and very comfortable chic boutique
text:
I’m so happy and satisfied with my stay that I’ve decided to compose my review even before my checkout. 

Paris is notorious for over priced minuscule boxed motels with terrible beds and decor. I was very fortunate to stumble upon this property and what attracted me most were the high ratings. 

As soon as you walk into the lobby you can feel the essence of Paris in this chic, boutique style hotel/reception. Sandy the receptionist has really made sure my stay has been extremely welcoming/comfortable . Sandy is friendly, thoughtful, speaks perfect English/French, works with her guests with whatever needs their might be and not once made me feel like I was ever asking for too much. Even if the lobby she’ll ask if I need anything or city map, she really increased the star level of the experience. Thank you! 

All the decor is a lovely chic motif. My own room appears out of an apartment in a style magazine for a room in Paris with the walls all lined in a velvety blue. Everywhere you walk the smells throughout the rooms and hotel are a fragrant clean smell. There is a working lift/AC. You can also open a window if you prefer. The bathrooms have showers and are spotless. The beds are very comfy and cater to those who prefer soft or firmer mattress, like Goldie Locks, it’s just right. 

You have the option for breakfast in the small cafe downstairs whether buffet or an express. A metro is close by. The blackout curtains ensure a great nights rest. Flat screen tv with CNN in English is always a plus on top of the coffee/tea kettle, safe a mini fridge. I am most impressed with the renovated decor as everything feels new and clean. 

Please bare in mind that this is Paris with buildings over 100s of years old and real estate sky rocketing. The only downsize for some will be the potential size of the room/hotel which you can see online. The elevator is also quite small but as long as you can lift your heavy luggage it shouldn’t matter! Think chic, intimate boutique style, newly renovated with lovely and helpful staff and voila you’re in Paris! 🍾

title: Nice stay but amenities lacking
text:
I need to preface that this is a fantastic hostel with lovely staff and upbeat/hip vibes. My room was clean, as was the hostel itself. It was decorated very cool, nice lounging areas and the rooftop is a huge bonus. 

Here are the negatives:
- no towels (they come rented, at a cost) 
-  no soap in any bathrooms (esp. during COVID!)
- no communal kitchen 
- no microwave/fridge 
- no cutlery (or like things you may need for dinner, utensils) 
- it gets VERY loud in the evenings with the music 
- Idk about all the rooms but my room had a mosquito every single night and it made sleeping impossible
- I was also on the top bunk and you cannot control the heat/cooling in the room, you have to go down, so I was constantly hot. 

The last 3 points are nitpicking, but expecting soap, towels and a kitchen is the BARE minimum out of a hostel experience (And I’ve been to many). 

I’d say this: If you score a really cheap deal here and can live without the above, absolutely do it. It was a fantastic stay, even with some of the inconveniences. But, if those inconveniences may irritate you, as much as they did me (and you can splurge elsewhere), I would say explore that option. Cause for me cooking dinner at home was essential for budgeting reasons and that was a huge impediment (but I guess it’s also on me for not pre-checking, but I never would have thought a hostel doesn’t have a kitchen - that’s like hostelling 101!)

title: Great location. Friendly staff. Good for family.
text:
I visited with my three kids in the peak of August. I primarily booked because of the central location, and the ability to have a family room which sleeps 4. 

The room was lofted, with me and my eldest sharing the ‘upstairs’. And my twins sharing the pull out. Beware that the bathroom is ‘open’. The toilet room has a door and the separate shower has a glass door, but the bath tub and the sink is open plan. Not an issue for us, but could be for some.  We didn’t spend much time in the room because we were out touristing. 

The proximity to the tourist shops and places to eat was a huge bonus. Some reviews have mentioned Street noise, but we did not find that troublesome at all. Maybe because we were in the 6th floor in the roof!  We did a LOT of walking (with three kids!), including back from the Eiffel Tower climb via Rodin and Musee D’Orsay. Very close to Tour boat departure, Sainte Chappelle and conciergerie. 

The front desk was exceedingly friendly. Excellent English. Smiled politely and listened to my halting French. They recommended easy RER/metro solutions  because of the disruption to some services at the local station. 

Would definitely recommend.

title: Very nice hotel in Latin quarter
text:

Since  we were on an early flight  we arrived at hotel around 10 am. Emma at the reception told us that she will provide us with a room for a small fee as soon as there’s a room available. She told us to leave our bags at hotel go for a little walk and came back in half hour.  When we came back an hour later she had a room for us!!!!

The room itself is a bit small but very comfy and cosy. Anyway this is Paris , in general almost every hotels comes with small rooms. The room was clean, bed was very comfy , washroom was very good with very good hot water pressure. We also had a little balcony for two in our room. Good Wifi.

Staff are very friendly. Emma was super friendly and very helpful not only with us but will the guess that I’ve seen her dealing with. So was the other guy who works at night as well as the trainees.

The location is one of my favorite whenever I’m in Paris. Everything is in walking distance. La Maison D’Isabelle  2nd prize for best croissant in 2018 and lots of restaurants and bistros. Easy walk to Le Louvre, Les Halles among others . Easy access to La Tour Eiffel, Paris CDG by RER and metro to other historical sites.

Overall we enjoyed our stay at the Hotel Europe Saint Séverin. Service is top notch. Thank you Emma thank you everybody.

By the way I’ve read some of the previous reviews that the  elevator is very small and can only fit  one person. It must have been the old one whiz is no longer in service . The new one can easily fit 4 persons . The hotel have a restaurant across the reception. However we didn’t eat there.

We will definitely go back to this hotel next time we are in Paris!!!

title: Great location
text:
Cute little place in the 5th. We chose this hotel due to its location. Our daughter lives around the corner. We opted for the suite since some of the regular rooms looked small on the web page and in Paris small rooms are fairly common.
The suite is two floors with  the bedroom upstairs. Its a very cute little place with a large tub and separate shower. The room is very clean and nice. 
The elevator to the floor seem to be broken so we took another set of elevators to the 5th floor and had to go up a flight of stairs to the 6th. The hallways on the 5th to cross to the other side was full of laundry bags and a large cart which made it a little more challenging with suitcases. Once in the room we were pleasantly surprised. You have everything you need. We are moving to a different location so we are spending only one night here. However it would definitely work for a longer stay. There are tons of restaurants, shops around and within walking distance to many well known attractions. Can’t beat the location. However, as in many parts of Paris parking will be a challenge if you have rented a car.

title: Perfect for a long weekend - breakfast is a must!
text:
Nice, clean hotel with quirky decor and everything you need for a long weekend in Paris. 

The aircon was amazing and kept the room cool the whole time - well needed when we visited during the heatwave! 

Very easy when travelling via Eurostar, hotel is directly opposite from Gare du Nord, which made the commute extremely pleasant. There is a Metro line outside which is handy for travelling. 

Could not recommend the breakfast here enough! If staying here, breakfast is a must - great range of choice from and high quality, well worth the extra. 

The only negative was that the area surrounding the hotel (train station) can be a bit busy and riff raff-y at night, but this didn’t really impact our stay and we walked back at night throughout our stay with no issues. Hotel is also very quiet so was easy to get a good nights sleep. Bed and pillows were extremely comfortable.

title: A fantastic place to stay for a long weekend in Paris
text:
the location couldn't have been more perfect - we jumped off the train, walked out the station doors and crossed the road right into the hotel! Check in was a breeze and we were heading up to our room via the quirky porter lift in moments. 

The room was brilliant and themed up in the an aesthetic similar to the orient express. Deep purples, luggage racks and quirky lighting. The rain shower room was a bonus we didn't expect too!

The room had air con which was incredible during the 35+ heatwave that was happening, and we loved reading through the brand story and neighbourhood book they left out on the bed too.

We paid for breakfast which i would highly recommend to everyone visiting. Plenty of food to choose from ranging from hummus and olives, bacon, eggs and french toast - or a mountain of different pastries and so on... well worth the extra cost to set you up for a morning of wandering the city!

The building itself was lovely and the artwork throughout made it feel very unique and comfortable. If you're looking for something quirky then this is it!

We also tried the terminus nord restaurant next door and the food was fantastic and the price  very decent for the quality sea food they serve!

title: Great hotel, great location for Eurostar terminal
text: I booked this hotel for 1 night when attending an Ed Sheeran concert in Paris. I didn’t get to the room until about midnight, and hadn’t been expecting a great deal, but on arrival I was pleasantly surprised by how lovely the room was, so it was a shame I hadn’t been able to spend more time there. I chose it for its location to Gare du Nord for the Eurostar terminal, which is literally right opposite, and was hugely convenient when having to get an early train from Paris to London.  It was impeccably clean, modern, and really unique in its styling. The staff were polite and friendly, and the bed was luxurious and comfortable. After having come from a tiny hotel room in London for the same price, I was shocked at how big the room was. I’d definitely stay here again if I’m ever in Paris. Great hotel.

title: Decent hotel
text:
Lovely hotel. We had a medium room and it was plenty bug enough for the two of us, king sized bed, double shower and lots of clothes hanging space. 

Drinks in the bar were lovely, clearly explained and all staff members spoke a decent level of English. 

Only disappointments were the food in the NENI restaurant, staff there did not speak clear English and couldn't understand the concept of gluten free - This shouldn't be a hard thing to grasp.

Also, there is a £100 per room per night security deposit, and a £7 per room per night city tax cost - Neither of these are explained at the point of booking and so you turn up to a pre booked space and have to pay them on the spot or you have no hotel room. They also advise you will get your £100 deposits back on check out, I asked and was told it had been refunded, now a day later I have still not received it. Such a shame as this and the staff/menu at NENI have brought the score down so much, it would have been a five star review had it not been for these two points.

Please improve.

title: Great location, very clean hotel
text:
We’ve just recently got back from spending 4 nights in Paris at this wonderful hotel. It’s in a great location directly opposite Gare de Nord train station, which is fantastic if you come on the Eurostar.
We had a medium double which was bigger than the normal double rooms I’ve stayed in in Paris. 
The room were they served breakfast was quirky and well laid out. We had champagne for breakfast every day with the usual French cuisine. There was also a hot choice for breakfast, but we chose ham,cheeses, croissants, baguettes, jam, fruit and yogurt. There is filter coffee available, however on request you can order lattes, espresso etc. 
The hotel has two lifts adjoined in reception,one is for a max of two people. There is also a lift that takes you to the dining area and bar. 
We will definitely be returning in the near future.

title: Reasonably priced and trendy hotel opposite Gare du Nord
text: I'd never heard of the 25 hours chain until recently and have just stayed in Berlin and Paris back to back. The chain is reasonably priced and trendy whilst being relatively no frills. This hotel is well situated opposite the Gare du Nord (brilliant for early trains and late sleepers) . The rooms are evocative of a bygone era of travel and Paris while being modern and comfortable. My room had a view of an internal courtyard and a shower not bath so if you want something different check what else the hotel has to offer. There's a trendy bar and levantine restaurant on the first floor. Oddly the restaurant has the same menu in Paris and Berlin and I have to say Berlin did it better but it was still fine (note for the management: the lunchtime staff in the restaurant gave great customer service). Minibar is free with water and beers on arrival. No kettle in the room which for a Brit was disappointing. Helpful and friendly reception staff. A credit card is taken on arrival for incidentals with a 50 euro preauthorisation. This was a business trip and one of my colleagues is used to staying in more upmarket hotels, despite that they were pleasantly surprised by the experience. I've stayed in other hotels near gare du nord and this was the best of the ones I've been at.

title: Just about figured everything out
text:
I just returned from 5 nights at Terminus Nord. As you might have already read, it is located directly in front of Gare Du Nord with an entrance to the Metro immediately in front of the hotel. The area around the hotel isn't great but that goes with the territory given that its near a train station. 

This is an enoromous hotel that somehow manages to feel intimate. The staff are friendly and all speak English. Our room was totally quiet and kitted out in a quirky mix of African art/textiles with some retro Indian effects. There are light switches everywhere but you eventually figure out what they are for. Great rainfall shower, good wifi, good air con, pretty comfy bed, and very clean. The room was a bit on the poky side but you are in central Paris, so there you go. The bar was cosy, dark and intimate. 

The only downside of 25 Hours (and I haven't downgraded their score as this is optional) was their eye wateringly expensive 24 Euro breakfast. We went around the corner to a glorious patisserie called 'Carton' and had their award winning croissants and inexpensive breakfast sandwiches. The coffee was just so so, but a very buzzy little place. Good luck!

title: Chosen at random but we came up trumps !
text:
What a wonderful place to stay.  My husband and I spent 3 nights here on a Eurostar trip that we had been trying to get to since 2020.  It’s great that it is right opposite Guar de Nord so no lugging case on the metro or into cabs when you arrive.  The hotel itself was very unique.  Great quirky rooms  with comfortable beds and fantastic shower facilities en suite.  Staff were lovely and cheerful and couldn’t do enough for you. Our room was on the 6th floor and was very quiet.  The main bonus for us was the breakfast.  It was absolutely fabulous.  Great hot and cold food with plenty of variety. Self serve so you could take your time. Copious amounts of continental fair including salami’s, ham, hummus and cheeses and of course a vast bread and pastry selection.  Fresh salmon and  scrambled eggs, bacon, sausages and French toast.  Cereal and yoghurt and a large fruit salad.  They even had champagne amongst the drinks to help yourself to.  What more do you need to fill yourself up for the day when you have sight seeing ahead.  We also tried the restaurant in the hotel on the Saturday night which was Israeli inspired and the food there was very good too.  Nice atmosphere with friendly waiters.  This hotel is situated well for using the metro too, it is literally o/s the hotel doors. There are plenty of other eateries around the hotel . 
The only negative for us was the amount of groups of young men and homeless sleepers hanging around the front of the train station and surrounding streets.  This is not a problem during the day but a bit nervy later in the evening.  Saying that it didn’t spoil  our visit and as I now know that this hotel is a chain I will definitely use them again in another city.

On arrival, in the reception area, this appears quirky. Checkin was quick and we went to our room. Room was small but, a nice view over a courtyard. 

The bathroom was three different sections. Toilet, next was shower and then a different section again was sink. This  was extremely quirky and decor was mismatched and artwork was made from recycled washing liquid. In a funny way, this all seemed to work. 

We had breakfast on both days and it was beautiful. Tea was made from real tea leaves, once you got your head around there was no tea bags. There was all hot and cold stations. Champagne was even available, which was a lovely addition. Croissants were fresh and frequently replenished. 
The breakfast room was busy on both days and this seems to be a poplar hotel despite its quirky appearance. All areas were cleaned and sanitised. I would go back but, would request a different room

The lifts were very small and congested at meal and check out time and having to wait a long time for one. This was perhaps the only thing we would complain about. They need to look at the lift situation

Local heroes serve as the inspiration for the interior design concept. The design agency Dreimeta collaborated with the Parisian team Visto Images to encapsulate the hustle and bustle of the 10th Arrondissement: A playful hodgepodge of vibrant, colourful wall murals in street-art style.

title: Amazing location, funky rooms, best start into Paris
text: I have been in Paris several times before and know how hard it is to get a decent hotel for a good price. 25Hours Hotel exceeded my expectations and all my recent Paris Hotel experiences. The design of the Hotel is typical for 25hours Hotels, but greatly adapted to a style parisienne. Lots of love into the details. The service was great. Everyone was really friendly and helpful. The rooms amazing, great size (we stayed in a room with balcony) and the location itself is perfect for a weekend city trip to Paris.

title: Brilliant stay in Paris
text:
This hotel is amazing! So convenient to Gare du Nord literally across the road handy for heavy luggage! If you’ve got a metro ticket just as easy to get around anyway and close to Montmatre.
Check in was great and we were upgraded to a bigger room which had two balcony facing the sacre coeur which was all lit up at night, we could actually sit out there and watch the world go by!
The bed was amazing! The shower was also amazing, proper hairdryer! 
We also had breakfast included which is actually forgotten about and that was great, you could even make a bucks fiZz for breakfast.
Just two minor niggles: No kettle. Would be really handy as us Brits just love a cup of tea in the morning. TV kept turning itself off. Otherwise we loved it here and can quite easily say it was one of the best hotels I’ve been in for a long while!!
We’ll probably be back later this year as the concert we came to see was rescheduled.

The hotel bar is a really nice place to hang out and the service is exceptional.  All in all a brilliant experience and would definitely return without hesitation.

text:
My first stay at the 25hours hotel Paris Terminus Nord, from the first impression walking through the door I had a great feeling for this hotel.  I received a very warm welcome from Ludovic who very kindly upgraded my room.  The room was amazing, certainly the one of the best rooms I’ve stayed in for a long time. The room was warm and welcoming, with lots of quirky features. The bed was huge and VERY comfortable, unfortunately I had to leave at 6:30am for an early Eurostar train. The hotel is a 2min walk to the station.
I had a meal in the hotel restaurant that was excellent with a really interesting menu.
The whole vibe of the hotel was spot on, I can’t wait to come back on my next trip to Paris.

title: Great value for money
text:
Situated in a gorgeous Parisian building right opposite Gare du Nord and metro network. Loved how the neighborhood, known for its African community, came back in the design - and not subtly, if I may say so ;-) Love how 25hours always creates a sense of place, which makes all their properties unique. 

We were upgraded to an attic room with gorgeous views on the Sacre Coeur and the tip of the Eiffel Tower. Shower and bathroom amenities were great. Bed was very big and comfortable. 

Big shout out to the staff: they were incredibly friendly, welcoming, and personal. 

Small points of criticism: Neni (restaurant) was closed during lunch and with that we were not even able to get a coffee to go while we were waiting for our room to be ready / train to depart. Some coffee / tea facilities in the room would also be great.

title: Fab hotel in a great location
text:
A great hotel with some really nice quirky touches.
The place had a real character which is a pleasant change from the normal soulless hotels chains.
The only reason we didn’t give a five star rating is due to the price of the breakfast (€24/person) which we thought was a bit greedy as was the price of drinks in the bar, but if the hotel chooses to charge this much, then there’s plenty of places locally where you can get breakfast for a fraction of the price. We just felt the hotel let themselves down charging these inflated prices to their guest, but as I say, there’s plenty more choice available only meters from the hotel
The hotel is perfectly located to explore Paris... there’s even a Metro entrance 5 paces from the front door.
We highly recommend this hotel, just be aware of the highly inflated beer and breakfast prices.

text:

However, as well as being colourful and funky the check in process was very easy, the room was a good size, very comfy and warm.  We also loved the eco touches with the large shampoo, shower gel etc (no plastic bottles to pinch), the bag we could use during our stay and mentions of saving water etc.  The breakfast was brilliant - lots of choice, both hot and cold and very efficient staff keeping everything topped up.

Looking forward to staying in one of their other hotels and would not hesitate to stay here again :)

title: Great little hotel!
text:
Firstly - location is excellent right next to metro access to town nice and easy. The neighbourhood is bustling and only a 10 min walk from Gare Du Nord so save some pennies and walk to your hotel. 

Bring earplugs just in case got room overlooking street as we had and you’ll be fine- glazing is good it does help with street noise.

Cheaper to eat out locally obviously than in town- nice couple of restaurants we tried near the canal one was Eritrean and the other Thai. Around £12 for a main. Check trip advisor. 

Room- we were given room 105. Have to admit little disappointed as it was dated, mattress wasn’t very comfortable I could feel springs and it really needs a refresh. However, had a little kettle was immaculately clean, tv. So very basic but clean. 

Service- excellent. Polite staff, accommodated our needs with meds needing to be stored in fridge for my husband. 

Food- breakfast was good. Very good choice- cold meats, cheese, yoghurts, cereal, breads, eggs to do to your own softness, hot drinks, fresh juice, fruits. Breakfast room kept lovely and clean. Nice little outside area we enjoyed starting our day here- was starting to get little chilly in mid sept but we wanted to eat out as much as we could. 

Hotel could improve by 1- clamping down on guests obviously smoking in rooms- this is very dangerous and they just need smoke alarms fitting in room to discourage this along with a designated smoking around outside the hotel. Never had this issue in any other hotel and it was disconcerting to say the least as I was immediately aware this put all guests and staff at risk in event someone left cigarette burning by accident at night. 

2 - upgrade beds in our room (105) and redecorate remaining rooms that need upgrading as this lets down the hotel as everywhere else is pleasant and modern to walk around. Suspect entire corridor was like this as corridor felt a bit old fashioned and dated with strong smell of cigarette smoke too.

title: Very Good
text: Excellent location! First day I had room with the door attached to other room. I didn't feel comfortable. Next day they changed that room. Mid night attendant (bearded guy) was amazing person with very good service. I didn't like the tallest attendant. I think he is manager and he was very rude. Ac was not good enough. But was ok.

title: Don’t stay here!
text: We checked in at midnight after flying half way across the world. In 30 minutes had killed multiple insects and were utterly disgusted with the burns in the carpet and dirty walls. Wouldn’t refund us.

title: Would recommend.
text: Staff were friendly. Rooms clean and newly decorated. Room change given on request as booked a double bed. Nothing was too. Much trouble. Near to tube station with excellent connections. Close-to eurotunnel station. Breakfast suitable

title: Too much noise inside hotel room
text:
Firstly the positives: the bed was very comfy, and the staff were extremely polite and hospitable. The teas and coffee provisions were satisfactory also.

However there were two concerns with our visit. The first was that there was a lot of noise at night inside the hotel room. There was noise outside, especially from sirens. However this was not a major issue. Unfortunately there was a whirring noise 24/7 coming from inside the hotel, even with the air con turned off. This was a disturbance getting to sleep, for which we were unable to do anything about.

The second concern was that the hotel breakfast was not particularly hygienic. The hotel doors were open into the garden, which meant that there were bugs (such as flies) coming into the area where the food was. Unfortunately there was uncovered food, such as croissants and salami, which was attracting these insects. These food should have been either covered in cling film, or stored in a tub of some sort.

title: Perfect location lovely hotel
text:
We had a lovely visit to Paris and stay at the Louis Blanc 
Clean and fresh with air conditioning and wonderfully comfortable beds after plenty of walking around and doing touristy things . 
1 minute walk from metro and perfect location to just wander around and enjoy cafe culture and soak up atmosphere 
Staff very pleasant and helpful 
One downside is we booked two rooms and paid an extra £43.00 for one of the rooms with a bath as my husband likes a soak to relax his back . This was a mistake as the bath was half size and he could not fit in it as he is over 6 ft so it just became an impossibly tight shower . 
In England I would have asked for this money to be refunded but unfortunately my French is not adequate enough to discuss this 
Please do not let this put you off the hotel is lovely

title: Excellent stay
text: Nice clean hotel in an area with lots of restaurants and public transport nearby. Staff is very friendly and open to answer questions. When we had a question about a restaurant, the guy at the reception called them for us. Good service!

title: Great hotel near the really vibrant canal area .
text:
Great hotel, size of room you would expect for such a good price, booked direct and got a better deal than any booking site, easy online check in , all staff were very  friendly , good size bed , balcony, excellent air con, room tidied bed linen and towels changed every day, 50 meters from metro,brilliant bakery opposite, supermarket 50 meters and 200 meters from the vibrant canal district with great bars and restaurants. A really good base will definitely come back if we can have the same room !!
I do get some people may not have had the same experience dependent on where they room was in the hotel  but I can only describe our great stay.

title: Great location, lovely hotel
text: Modern design, helpful staff.  Rooms modern but small.  Wet room large and lovely and clean.  Location great, opposite Metro with some nice restaurants, bakery and fruit shops within 50 m. Air con really useful in heat of the summer

title: Excellent
text: Excellent hotel and lovely staff. Friendly, subway, clean, good breakfast, good location, silence, not expensive, good rooms. We will come back as soon as possible.  20 minutes walk from Gare du Nord station.

title: Good stay for a low price
text: Good stay for a good price. Nice hotel, good service and a nice room. Location is also very good. Your really close to al the attractions. Would recommend if you are looking for a hotel that isn’t expensive.

title: Very enjoyable 5 night stay in Paris
text: Hotel is in an ideal location, being only a 15 minute walk from Gare Du Nord station and having a metro station just across the street. Also plenty of shops and two very pleasant bistros / bars within a shot walk which we visited. Hotel room was very clean and had everything we needed for our stay. Continental breakfast was also very good particularly with the option to sit in the courtyard garden. Hotel staff were all very friendly and attentive and happy to provide any assistance or advice during our stay. Would highly recommend and would definitely consider returning for a further visit.

title: Hotel Louis Blanc
text:
Really lovely staff at reception, friendly and knowledgeable.
Great location to explore Paris with 2 metro stations on your doorstep.
Interesting area with all local amenities close by.
Highly recommended.

title: Great stay close to public transport
text:
