title: Why stay anywhere else?
text: I arrived after a long haul from Australia & the staff tried very hard to prepare my room early. All staff were welcoming & provided good advice throughout my 9 day stay. My special thanks to the hard working ladies in the kitchen. I stayed in a comfort double room which was small but this is typical for Europe. It was clean & comfortable with double doors leading to a balcony facing the Boulevard - great for people watching. The only noise was the church bells that do start early. The bathroom was small but modern with plenty of towels & contained the best amenities I found in all of Europe.  The shower floor is slippery when wet so be careful. The lift is the smallest I have ever seen - 1 person & 1 bag! Avoid if you are claustrophobic. However, I never had to wait. Breakfast is in the basement & offers an  unchanging menu consisting of the usual cold meat, cheese & croissants but also fresh eggs & bacon. The cafe noir is excellent. The stairs down to the basement are very steep so take the lift if you have mobility issues. The location is a draw card. Even at my pace Notre Dame is 5 minutes walk. The Hop On/Off bus leaves from the front of ND so this is a gateway to all of Paris. The metro is also close. There is a laundry across the street opposite the church. Carrefours Express is across the street to the right & sells most items of need plus wine at reasonable prices. Also on the right is a bank, pharmacy & tabac plus La Patisserie which I highly recommend. It is the only alternative that I found to hotel breakfast. There are 2 restaurants either side of the hotel. The green cafe is bistro fare  & not very good. The red one is a Basque restaurant which is good if you love loads of meat & rich sauces. I recommend the Twickenham which is about 450 metres to the right. Great food. My criticisms are few but worth mentioning. The mini fridge is too small to hold a wine bottle so had to be unloaded first & their were no wine glasses. It's not a big deal but this is France after all. The biggest inconvenience was the location of the power socket behind a very heavy desk near the floor. I have arthritis & could not access it so the lovely hotel maid did it for me. However, it should not be assumed that everyone is capable of crawling around on their knees to plug in devices. My stay was comfortable & safe. If I am lucky enough to go back to Paris I will definitely stay here again. Merci Beaucoup.

text: Great location, easy access to Metro and walking distance to many places.  Go over to La Fayette roof top for beautiful view of Eiffel Tower.  Staff was very helpful and pleasant.  Room updated, comfortable and clean.  Will stay here again.

They allowed my son to check in his large backpack when we first arrived because it was earlier than our check-in time. That was much appreciated!

title: Trois nuits à Paris
text:
A good hotel with friendly staff in the centre of Paris.
We walked to the Louvre, the Casino and all the restaurants we visited.  
The breakfast buffet was very good and diverse.
At night we closed the window to the street, but could open another one to the court, where it's really quiet.

title: great
text: excellent location, enough space in room, and breakfast served! We had a triple room, and it was excellent, not a tiny one, as we usually had in Paris. Everyhting was perfect, except the fact that the walls between the rooms are too thin, and one night was therefore restless, as we had noisy nabours.

title: Good accomodation
text:
Nice room and service with reasonable price.
The location was pefect, just next to theGaleries Lafayette and  easy to get everywhere  in Paris using subway.
I enjoyed staying there thanks to the good hospitality too.
Thanks for

title: Great location
text:
Location is great! Just one street behind H&M, Lafayette. Easy access to shops, sights, cafes etc.
Stayed 2 nights in single room and returned for 3 more nights in superior room. The single room is small especially with the tiny bathroom which is pretty challenging to navigate. However the room is not facing street, which makes the room totally silent great for a good night’s sleep. The superior room is more spacious as compared but poor sound proofing for some reason could hear next door guests talking, water flashing etc. Such a shame for paying more for a “better” room.

title: Perfect Hotel in Paris
text: The hotel was perfect for our purpose (1 week family holiday, 2 adults and one minor of 6 years). The location is very central and in a very attractive neighbourhood of Paris. The staff at the hotel was exceedingly nice and among the friedliest staff I have come about in any hotel. Dining options are many nearby (especially Asian) and the underground line is just around the corner. I can only think of one negative aspect, which however is true for more or less all hotels in Paris: street noise at night. Still, the whole family slept with an open window peacefully every day from 10:30 p.m. to 6:30 a.m. next morning (thanks to an exciting and eventful day). I will not think twice when coming back to Paris and will book this hotel again without hesitation.

title: Good Lolcation

 The opera is also close and many more attractions as  well.

Nice to stay.

title: Great hotel
text: We had a lovely stay at this hotel! Rooms were clean and the location is amazing. Very easy to walk to Montmartre and towards les Toulleries and around the Opera area. Would definitely recommend a stay here.

title: Good location and staff
text: Good location close to shops, restaurants and train stations. Galery Lafayette is just next door and very convenient. The staff is very kind and welcoming. Just watch the steps when leaving the elevator.

title: nice stay
text: Had a great stay here! The staff, particularly Jean-Marc, were wonderful, the location was perfect, and the breakfast was delicious. Very convenient location for my work trip to Paris. Absolutely would stay here again!

title: Enoyable Stay December 2021
text: Good 3star hotel in a great location, suitable for couples and small families - close to the big department stores and metro station, lots of options for eating and shopping. The staff are all very warm and friendly and speak English. Room is barely big enough to swing a cat in - but who comes to Paris to stay in the room?  The hotel overall is clean but could do with some renovation work to modernise it and to make it even better.  We had a room at the top floor so we had a great view. Would certainly use this hotel again for future holiday trips.

title: Highly recommended

The hotel and room was clean.
We Will return for sure on our next trip to Paris. 
Thank you

title: Great location
text:

Requested high floor for our 5 day stay, as expected busy road to be noisy. 5th floor room was perfect with typical long windows opening onto pretty small balcony overlooking rue Lafayette. title: Great value

title: wish I stayed longer at this hotel!

I have just spent 4 nights in your lovely hotel. The room was clean and the staf very friendly and had good costumer service. The best thing is the lokation, next to Metro and shopping!
All in all a very nice stay!

title: My favorite in Paris
text: Excellent service, cleanliness and friendliness. The people are very friendly like Oliver and Juan Marco.  They speak spanish too. The breakfast is good and the cleanliness of the rooms excellent and very nice location.

title: recommended
text: This hotel gives us a warm feeling. All the staffs are really nice and friendly giving good advice.The location is perfect, close to Galeries Lafayette and is in the center of the city. Also, it’s clean.

title: Fabulous Central Location, Super Service & Excellent Value
text:
Located in the Opera neighborhood and right next to the major and famous department stores Gallerie Lafayette & Printemps, shopping high-end or fast fashion (H&M) are all nearby.  I also walked to the Louvre, Champs-Ellyses, Grande Palais, Gare de l'Est, Passage Verdeau, etc., (during the recent strike in Paris which brought the subways to a halt for many days). I would shop for awhile than go back to my hotel (a short walk) drop of my bags and then go back out again. It was extremely convenient. There are many restaurants in the area and a couple of grocery stores. I happen to love Chinese food and there are many decent ones nearby. You can also go into the Gallerie Lafayette l'epicerie, their specialty, wine and food shop and grocery store. There you can grab delicious snacks for hotel room and peruse all the differnt ethnic and special French pastries, chocolates, cheeses, etc.. Its sooo yummy!  
All of the staff behind the front desk are all friendly, professional and very accomodating. They speak English well and are happy to answer questions. They quickly remembered my room number and had my key ready anytime I walked through the door.  They will tend to any concerns or requests very promptly.  They are the other great feature of this hotel. 
The room and facilities are very clean and up-to-date. My single room was like a dorm-room, small for sure, but  it was all I needed since I didnt spend much time in my room anyways.  My room was always very clean and well stocked with snacks, towels etc.. The only thing I had trouble with was the temperature, I was always really hot. I was just there in early December, my room was on the top floor so perhaps the heat from lower floors helped to raise the temp in mine, but I had to have them completely turn off the heat and in addition sleep with the bathroom window open to feel comfortable. It was very hot in my room. But it was pretty quiet up on the top floor which helped make sleep more sound. 
Overall this hotel with is reasonable rates and all the above mentioned makes this hotel an overall excellent value.

title: Great Location and charming hotel
text: Less than a five minute walk the Garnier Opera House and the Paris Metro, this was the perfect location. The rooms are small, but clean and safe. My only complaints were that 1) the room wad to hot with no easy ro adjust the temperature.  Fortunately I could open the window,  and the chill air mixed ro make the room very comfortable. 2) It was strange to have to  leave the key anytime I left the hotel,  and once I had ro wait about two minutes just to get back in. But all said,  I would definitely return.

title: Hotel Exelsior Opera
text:
Friendly reception. 
Clean rooms, located close to the Galerie Lafayette and Printemps. Walking distance to Gare St. Nazare and Metro station Opera. Several restaurants surounding the Hotel such as Italian, Indian, Chiness, Japanese etc.

title: Paris for 2 Days
text: Nice comfortable stay for 2 days here. Enjoyed location with easy walk to metro 9 with straight line to Eiffel Tower Trocadero. Easy walk to beautiful Garnier Opera house and Galleria Lafayette plus convenient walk to catch hop on hop off bus nearby. Museums nearby as well. Small elevator but air temp was comfortable with affordable balcony from room.

title: Super helpful staff and comfortable room
text:
The room with the king size bed was actually a little more spacious than a typical city center hotel in Paris. Having the free bottled water was convenient for everyday travel. The towels were good quality. We didn't use the elevator often but if you have big bags, it might be hard to squeeze in with multiple people. One of the best things about the hotel was the helpful staff. I left a personal item in the room when checking out, and had to call the hotel to tell them to keep it for a few weeks until I returned to Paris to pick it up. Each time I communicated with them, I got a courteous reply. Sure enough, I was able to claim my item during my very brief return to Paris the night before flying out of CDG. 
The location is very convenient with the Roissy bus within a few minutes' walk. Metro and RER stops are also nearby. Restaurants are simply too many to choose from.
I took one star out because of two things: (1) I don't like the anti-theft hangers (but a lot of hotels use them). (2) The walls are extremely thin. The next door neighbors just talked in their normal voice and it's as if they were talking in your room.

title: Location is good, but room size is small, worst thing is the shower water is really really small
text: Location is good, but room size is small, worst thing is the shower water in our room is really really small, the shower room door is not working properly in friend's room and their water is also small. Lucky we only stayed for one night.

title: Beautiful Paris
text: The hotel is located in a great area of Paris for shopping, restaurants etc. within walking distance to the Eiffel Tower, Mulon rouge, etc. the bed was very comfortable and the hotel staff was amazing. There are some things that need upgraded but the staff makes up for everything

title: Pro & Con
text:
Pro
Great location situated very near Gallery LaFayette and Printemps.  
Nearest metro station is less than 3 min walk.  
Taxi fare by meter cost Euro 10 from Gare du Nord train station to the hotel.
Supermarket just beside the hotel.  Can get bakery there.  Plenty of restaurants within the vicinity.
Hotel lobby and lift are dated but glad my room is furbished and clean.
Friendly hotel staff who speak English.

Con
As per the staff at the Reception, normal taxi fare (if you flag along the road) from Hotel to CDG airport cost around Euro 50.   However, if we need the hotel to book in advance and arrange for a taxi, it will cost Euro 65.  My friend and I decided to get the hotel to arrange the taxi as we are leaving early morning at 6.30am.  Unfortunately, when we arrive at the airport, the taxi driver insisted that the fare is Euro 77 and not 65!  We felt cheated but yet there is nothing we can do as we are leaving the city.  Very disappointed with the arrangement between the hotel and the driver.

title: Guillermina Torres de Betancourt

The room and bathroom were very clean, nevertheless the rugs at the hotel look dirty, which give a bad impression when we get there. I think you have to change that, could be another kind of floor. Wood would be nice, but probably too expensive.....there has to be a solution.

Kind staffs 
Elevator

Good room condition / cozy

title: Nice location

title: 3 nights in Paris
text: My husband, myself and my 20 month old daughter slept there for 3 nights.Overall it was a nice stay. The room was well located and clean but really small (especially with a cot inside). Staff was friendly and helpful.

title: Excellent and pleasant stay

title: Great location, room a bit small and noisy

A bit noisy although happy with this given location.  Friendly staff.  Hotel slightly tired looking but clean regardless.  We didn't eat breakfast here so can't comment

title: A most wonderful stay at most professionally run hotel!
text: I have stayed in quite a few hotels in Paris and never have I had the privilege of staying in a hotel that provided me with such great and excellent customer service! Where can I begin?  The front desk personnel were fabulous, providing us with great tips in respect to places to visit and eat in Paris that I was unaware existed!  The dining area was impeccable matching the wonderful personnel ensuring that our breakfast was one that for me excelled all expectations respecting hotel meal service!  I can not but say the entire experience for us (we stayed longer than a week) was phenomenal and exceptional!  Merci mille fois pour tout!  Thank you so much for everything!  I wish I could have stayed longer. I can but highly recommend this hotel, it goes above and beyond any other surrounding hotels where I have stayed in the past!  Bon travail!  Great job goes out to the entire staff!  We will return soon!

title: Good location! Good people!
text:

Elevator is good for 1 person and 2 luggages only but its okay coz our room is located at the 1st floor. The only weird thing is a vibrating sound every few minutes either elevator, subway or something i forgot to ask.

The front desk personnel of the hotel is accommodating and helpful, for me that helps make our Paris stay better.

text: This hotel is superbly located. The hotel has friendly staff and is clean and nice. The view from our room was to the impressive Opera building. The breakfast selection was small but good. We also had a smaller bathtub

title: excellent location
text: Location is excellent.  Quiet but close to metro and shopping area.  Restaurants are nearby. Staffs are very nice and helpful. The rooms we stayed have 4 large windows and a balcony. Very good view. However, might need to do a bit more on security check. Reception requires us to leave the key everyday when we go out.  However, the first night we came back and by mistake mentioned the wrong room number, and we got other room's key easily without verification. Suggest asking at least the last name for verification.

title: Wonderful hotel
text: The hotel is clean and kind. There is air conditioner so it's always cool. The breakfast is not free, but it is not bad to pay for it. I wish to stay in Excelsior Opera again, when I get back to Paris.

title: Very cute Paris hotel
text: We spent 4 nights here in June 2019. We did enjoy our stay. The hotel is located right next to Galleries Lafayette and next to a metro stop. It is next to a very cute and delicious Italian restaurant. There is a also a bakery where we got croissants one morning and a creperie right across the hotel. Very convenient location. It is a smaller room, but this is Paris. It was just my husband and myself, so we were fine. The rooms were very clean, and the staff at the concierge desk was so friendly.

title: Great service and friendly staff
text: Great service and friendly staff. Recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to Paris.  The location is close to shopping mall, high end shops, H&M, a grocery store, metro and awesome restaurants. The staff also provides daily room cleaning.

title: Fabulous!
text: This lovely hotel is located very near the metro which made travel around Paris very convenient. Our room was clean (but small as most European rooms are). The hotel is air conditioned which was so welcome after sightseeing in this heatwave. We also loved the Italian restaurant on the ground floor. We will stay here again and gladly recommend this hotel to friends.

title: such a great find!
text:
We loved this place -- welcoming, modern lobby, the room was comfortable and air-conditioned, beds were great, the bathroom was very modern and stylish with tiles and a pebble border.  Everything in the hallways and room felt new and comfy, there was a nice minibar, nougat snacks on the pillows. 
 The neighborhood has a great restaurant across the street and one next door, and all reasonably close to Gare St. Lazare. I can't say enough about the front-desk staff!  We were trying to find a TV to watch the Women's World Cup -- they scanned the TV in their bar area to see what station it might be on, then, when they figured out it was only on pay-sports stations and not available in the hotel, got us across the street to Le Royal, and they put it on their restaurant TV!

title: Nice people make your stay even nicer
text: Centrally located, amazing staff and clean place to stay in. We were very happy with our decision to stay at Hotel Excelsior Opera and would stay there again. There is so much around that there was not a minute of boredom.

title: Best location, but bad bathroom
text:
Location was really good.
I was able to arrive at a major tourist destination in about 15 minutes.
However, room smell and bathroom were not good.
We did not complain because of the problem of language communication, although the toilet sink was clogged from the time when we entered and water did not come down.
The staff was very kind.

title: 3 Nights in Paris
text:
Reasonably priced deal for a 3 night stay with breakfast. Everything is clean and tidy. This is a small hotel located near the opera house and and 1-2 minute walk from the Chaussee d’antin-La Fayette metro station. It’s very convenient to get to all the popular places either by train or walking. The lift in the hotel is amusingly small but goes with the character of the place. If you’re tired from all the exploring & couldn’t be bothered to look for true French cuisine for dinner, the Italian restaurant next door is very good. 
Nice no nonsense place to stay. I will use again.

title: Very Nice Hotel
text:
This hotel is perfect for a couple.  If you are going with more than 2 people, i wouldn't recommend this hotel as the rooms are small (like most European rooms).  The hotel is within walking distance from Gallaries Lafayette and the Opera. Perfect location with plenty of restaurants nearby. 

The room was very clean and was maintained everyday.  

This hotel is a boutique hotel.  There is not a lot of amenities, so keep that in mind when booking.  Don't expect a huge lavish lobby with a 5 star restaurant.  

Last thing:  This was a little weird, but you have to leave your key at the front desk when leaving.  You'll get it back when you return.  They say it's for security reasons, but I would feel more secure with keeping my key. What's stopping the front desk from giving my key to the wrong person?  My suggestion would be to upgrade to the key card system instead of an actual key.

Nevertheless, nothing happened, and we had a pleasant stay.

Paris Recommendations:  

1) Get a Metro Pass.  You will save a lot of money from Taxi's or Ubers.  Also, don't buy the pass from the machine.  Go to the "live" person behind the window to make sure you get the right pass. If you've every ridden on any public subway system, then you'll learn it in 5 minutes.  Look at the map and follow the line number.  the key is making sure that you know where you are and what direction you are going.  The direction you are going in is determined by the last stop on each end of the line. 

2) Most of the Cafe's are for happy hour and people watching. The real restaurants usually open at 7 and require reservations.  Do what the locals do and eat at the real restaurants.  Just ask the front desk for recommendations. Terrace Perruche is a fabulous restaurant overlooking the city in Printemps Mall. This is perfect as you can see the Eiffel Tower and all of the city while you eat. 

3) Eiffel Tower: Make lunch reservations at Restaurant 58.  This is the best way to skip the line and get access to the tower.  

4) Versailles Palace:  Make breakfast reservations at the Orr Restaurant.  Again, you'll be able to skip the line, and the breakfast is not that bad. This is outside of Paris and requires a separate ticket.  Be sure to purchase it from the window.

5)  Book in advance.  We booked all of our visits in advance through Viator.com.  Very easy, and you pay in USD. Get it out the way before you go. 

6)  Paris has over 10 million people. But unlike New York or Chicago, the city "sleeps."  Parisians leave the happy hour and they go to dinner and actually have conversations with each other.  So you'll see the streets empty at around 9 or 10.  

7)  Waiters and Waitresses do not hound you. This is because it is a "non-tipping" culture.  For them, they feel like they are interrupting you.  So don't be put off if you have to call them over to your table to place your order. That's intentional.  Again, Parisians use the time in restaurants as a time to connect.  So the atmosphere is extremely light.

Hope this review has helped someone.

title: Centrally located, needs some updates
text:
This hotel is centrally located. About a one minute walk to the Chaussée d’Antin-La Fayette metro stop. Super close to ALL shopping and to the Opera. 

The rooms need some updating. Carpeting was old, and the rooms don’t feel fresh. Bathtubs in all double and triple rooms are really high, keep that in mind if traveling with someone older. 

Breakfast was good, we came late and they made us some fresh eggs. A little pricey at 14 euros a person, but a good way to start the day. 

The front desk staff are helpful, especially Ernesto who accommodated us with another room at the last minute.

title: Lovely Hotel
text: We stayed at this hotel and it was great. The rooms are clean and the staff is very friendly and always eager to help. The location is perfect :very close to the subway. There are many cafes and a well-supplied minimarket nearby. If I ever return to Paris I would definitely choose this hotel again.

title: Great location and value
text:
This 3 star hotel is located very close to Galleries Lafayette. The staff are very helpful and kind. 

We enjoyed the breakfast a lot. Scrambled eggs, a few varieties of cheese and croissants were delicious. They charge 14 euros per person for the breakfast 
if you didn’t buy it inclusive.

Our rooms were slightly small, but that is the norm in Euro hotels. From 
October to April, you can find very reasonable prices. Especially on summer, prices go up significantly.

We were pretty satisfied with the location, staff and cleanliness (compared to others in Paris).

title: Very good
text: Very nice kind helpful staff.the rooms are vety clean.location is good.very close to metro station, galleries la fayette and opera garnier.breakfast is good too.there are cafe restaurants and a market close to the hotel.

title: Absolutely fantastic!
text:
We've stayed at the Hôtel Excelsior Opéra this week and I have nothing wrong to say about it!
The location is perfect, there's a metro stop about 1 minute walk away which is really good for commuting around the city. Gare du Nord is about 20 minute walk, in case you cannot be bothered with the public transportation. The street itself is quite central but very quiet at nighttime. 
The room was very clean with everything we needed and more. The staff is very nice and helpful.
We will definitely return to this hotel again!

title: Cute hotel in Oprah area
text: Location was the best! Room was tiny, elevator also tiny and cute. The room was average trough; don’t expect same value as you’d get at USA. We didn’t order breakfast so can’t tell anything about that.

title: Highly recommended!
text: The Hotel is a short walking distance to the train  and bus station of Big Bus, Airport shuttle and Paris Nord. We stayed in a triple sharing room with a corner view of Rue Lafayette.   Room and Bath are clean, beds are comfortable and the location is exceptional.  I will definitely stay here again.

title: B
text: Stayed for four nights. Very comfortable room on 5th floor with balcony. Breakfast was plentiful with good choice. All the staff were very polite and  helpful.  Great location with nearby metro and Rer stations so getting around was easy, even including to Disney.. 45 mins on rer. Another plus is the roissybus opera direct from cdg stop is very easy walking distance. Would definitely stay here again.

title: Very well located and practical
text: Nice rooms with amazing amenities, clean and comfortable beds. Staff was very nice as well. Only downsize is the limited space and the very small corridors and lift. But I believe this is due to the fact that the hotel is in an old (refurbished) building. Will definitely come again.

title: Comfortable, Great Value
text:
I stayed here for only a single night on a business trip. I have had bad experience with Paris hotels, but my room at Excelsior was larger than expected and the bed was extremely comfortable - it helped me stave off the jet lag :)

Would absolutely stay at this hotel again.

title: Highly recommendable Hotel
text:
I can highly recommend the hotel! 
Staff is just great! Very, very friendly and at your service! Felt very welcome and at home, especially traveling alone.
The single rooms are very small, but after all ‘t is Paris. Never the less the room was very well organised.
But still have 2 remarks about the room:
- Too warm and the a.c. not cooling down enough
- The minibar far from cold
The first night had trouble sleeping because I could hear and feel the subway under need up till third floor, but got used easily.
The breakfast offered enough choice and the fresh flowers on the breakfast tables were highly appreciated.
But I missed some background music at breakfast. If you find youself all alone, the silence is uncomfortable…
The location is great !
So definitely come back to stay at Excelsior Hotel next time I come to Paris or in meantime recommend it to my relatives.

title: All was ok during my stay in the hotel
text:
No complaints at all
All the employees were fantastic
On top of that, is very well placed close to the big and best shops in Paris.
Restaurants around make also life easy when you are in this hotel
Seriously, I will be back

title: Perfect 3* hotel!
text:
One of the best 3* hotels we stayed in. Air conditioning worked perfectly, the room was spacious, hotel’s staff was competent and friendly. Special thanks to Marie!

Sleep quality was very good, too. Our windows were facing a quiet street.
We would not hesitate to book the hotel again.
description: The Moderne Saint-Germain Hotel offers you a very central base for exploring Paris. Discover a district steeped in history with numerous major landmarks, including the Pantheon, the Luxembourg Gardens and Museum, Saint-Sulpice Church or the old Sorbonne University. Meander through the charming little streets of the Latin Quarter, rich with galleries, typical cafes and restaurants before you reach the Seine River and its romantic banks, the Ile de la Cité and Notre-Dame Cathedral.

title: Excellent Hotel, Staff, Great Location
text: We have stayed at The Hotel Moderne twice since 2019. We keep coming back because we like everything about this hotel. It is very clean, comfortable, reasonably priced, has wonderful front desk staff, and is in a superb location. The area is just down the street from the Pantheon, up from Blvd. Saint Germain and near Notre Dame with many very good bistros on the block and a lively student energy from the nearby schools giving the ancient area fa timeless energy. The hotel rooms are very lively in varied colors and wallpaper patterns and have good lighting with some creative aspects including different colors if desired. The rooms are very clean, the beds are comfortable, the wifi and TV are great, the bathrooms very clean and stylish with strong water pressure and a towel heater on the wall. We really appreciated as well the abundance of electric outlets in the room for charging phones and camera a laptop, etc. Both times we had the Superior Twin room at the end of a hall on the front of the hotel and the rooms were quiet. This is a non-smoking hotel. They stayed open during all of the pandemic and are very alert to all Covid issues and have a plexiglass panel in front of the reception desk. All of the front desk staff speak several languages including English, and in particular I very much appreciated Marie, Anaide, and Rudy, all of whom were exceptionally friendly and very helpful. They have a nice breakfast for only 8 Euros and they have coffee, tea and cold drinks available all day. When you leave the hotel they will ask you to give your key to the front desk and they will give it to you when they return; there is someone at that reception desk 24/7. So no worries there. The air conditioning is excellent which was much appreciated in the mid-June heat. Metro stops are within two blocks, and taxis and buses are right outside the hotel easily available.  There are markets and  shops all around and anything you need you can easily find. Also lots of bookstores in this literary neighborhood. This is a hotel we will keep coming back to in Paris and I look forward to doing so again.

title: Moldy Shower Put Downer on Otherwise Good Stay
text:
I hate to say I was a bit disappointed by our stay. It wasn't terrible by any means; I think I just had high expectations based on the very high score on here and on Google. It could just be that we were in the worst room in hotel (based on everyone else raving about their rooms!). I'd recommend against room 12 if you can help it. 

The pros:
-The day staff at the desk downstairs were very friendly- always greeted us when we came and left. 
-The location was very close to the metro and to a train to get to/from the airport. It was about an hour walk to the Eiffel Tower.
-There was a 24 hour desk, which was good since we arrived very late due to a delayed flight. The night clerk didn't seem thrilled to have to deal with our check-in, but he was helpful enough. 
-Bed was comfortable 
-Water pressure was great in the shower
-Towel heater in the bathroom was very effective and managed to dry all our clothes after we were soaked to the bone in an expected thunderstorm. 

The cons:
-The mold in the shower was my number 1 complaint. I don't ask for a lot in a hotel- mainly a clean bed and a clean shower, but the mold on the shower floor right where we stood grossed me out. I did mention it to the front desk when we checked out. The hotel was full while we were there, so I didn't bring it up earlier since it wasn't something that could be fixed immediately and there wasn't another room to move us to. There was also mold on the wall grout where we hung our towels. Maybe this isn't a major issue for others though. 
-The breakfast room was a bit small and was packed every day when we went down. We ended up just grabbing a croissant in a napkin to bring back up to the room. There are lots of bakeries nearby that are a much better option- just wish we hadn't paid for the breakfast. 
-There wasn't a Do Not Disturb sign, so the cleaning staffed knocked on the door each morning and came in regardless of whether we need anything that day. We would've preferred someone not come into the room each day when we were out. 
-The hairdryer worked for 11 seconds before needing a break to cool off. I mentioned it to the front desk, who said this was an intentional safety feature. They did say there was a hairdryer at the front desk that I could come down and borrow each day, but that felt like a hassle. Instead I'd dry my hair in 11 second spurts-- give it 2-3 mins to cool off, 11 more seconds...get fed up and decide damp was good enough. The hairdryer could only be used on the hottest setting, so there wasn't an option to just use it on a lower/cooler setting. If you do find yourself in this boat, after it shuts off, wait til you hear it click and then it's ready for another 11 seconds of use. Sometimes you might get a whole 15 seconds.

title: Great Location!
text:

The only thing I was not a fan of (and noticed this in other places so may be just a cultural difference) is that the heater was on in the breakfast area when it was 20 C( 70F) outside so it made it a little too warm for us, but the breakfast server was great. 

Would also high recommend going to La Petite Périgourdine  which is on the same block for dinner (great service and food) as well as Maison FOREST on the same street for coffee/pastries. The pastries were so good. 

Special shout out to Marie. She was the first person we met and she was great. She laid everything out and gave us some really good food recommendations and made us feel super welcomed. She was also the person that checked us out and let us know about the benefit of the room we had as we had one of the larger rooms in the hotel. Which is super good to know for next time. Room 57 if you're interested. It's super big for a Paris hotel!

title: Forgot laptop in hotel room… staff can’t find it…
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed for one night (4/27) at this hotel before departing for our flight home the next day. When we checked in we took some things out, including my boyfriend’s laptop which he uses for work. It stayed in the room the entire time. After watching a show on it in the evening, I placed it under the bed, so not to step on it, on the right side, barely sticking out. 

In the morning, we regrettably forgot to pack it and only realized we had left it in the hotel room when we arrived at the airport. Upset with having forgotten it, we were hopeful the hotel could hold it for us and could arrange to ship it. After calling to ask to check for it in our room, 26, the front desk clerk Marie, informed us it was not there. Confused, my boyfriend asked them to check the entire room, move the bed over etc. Quite frankly, it would be hard to miss seeing a 14 inch-sized silver hp laptop under the bed.

After a bit of back and forth calls from the airport, another woman from the hotel simply told my boyfriend they went to look through the room with the maid and didn’t find anything. The laptop has a GPS tracker (the battery is now dead) which showed that it was still at the hotel…

My boyfriend and I are very upset and confused at how his laptop has just “disappeared” and would like to further investigate with management. An otherwise nice stay at this hotel has turned our experience sour after this ordeal.

title: Second stay, still good
text:

The nice, fluffy slippers that used to await you in your room after check-in are gone now, and the water glasses have been replaced by plastic ones. Also, no more all-day espresso and croissants that used to be available in the downstairs lounge - gone, probably due to Covid. Still, we were happy there, especially in our 6th floor room that had a tiny terrace with a nice view. All the rooms are small but have plenty of storage space.. 

One negative: the rooms are frequently not cleaned until later afternoon/early evening which makes coming home for a break in the afternoon, especially on a hot day, to take a shower, change and relax before heading out again a bit problematic. 

Would stay there again.

title: My home away from home!
text:
I never thought I could stay over 3 months in the same hotel, but I was in Paris during the COVID crisis, and was lucky to book Hotel Le M Saint Germain, since it was one of the few hotels that continued to remain open. 

The first things I noticed was the chic and modern style of the hotel, and how each room has a different theme. I spent my first few weeks in a red room on the 3rd floor, and I absolutely loved it. My favorite part of the room was the huge bathroom.

On my third month, the staff upgraded me to a double room with a balcony on the 6th floor. It was bright, and had a fantastic view of the 6th floor, I quickly made this room my home.

The place is very tidy, and staff are always so accommodating and friendly, and they treated me like family. I especially enjoyed the chats getting to know the team (Marie, Anaide, Rudy & Krosky at the reception), as well as Nicole, the extra friendly lady who would tidy the rooms.
The hotel location (5th arrondissement, few minutes away from Notre Dame) and with great metro access was a huge relief.

I felt so at home at this hotel, that every time I come to Paris in the future, I will make sure I stay here. I definitely recommend.

title: A 3-star hotel that is worth a 1000-star review
text:
I went to paris from Nov 21st to Nov 27th, and stayed at Le M Saint Germain, after a lot of research and almost booking with a Mercure one. And I must say, I could not be happier that I chose them.

Upon arrival, on a rainy wednesday afternoon, I was received by Marie at the reception, who took care of my check in, giving my advices and tips to get around Paris, as well as explaining rules and functioning of the hotel itself. Kindly, I was informed that the room I could not have been given the room I had asked due to different categories, but that I was put into the most similar one corresponding to my category.

Proceeding to my room on the 2nd floor, I took the elevator, which is fairly small (3 to 4 people, no bags, is the maximum it can handle). Room 24 is in front of the elevator, and is pretty straightforward: a double bed, a desk with a chair and minibar, a closet, window with balcony, A/C, heater and wall-mounted TV. As for the bathroom, bear in mind you are in Europe, and especially in Paris, so space is not really a plus (except you're willing to pay 400€ /day). A shower, toilet, sink with blow dryer and rack to hand towels, all the essential. A kit with shampoo, body gel and body moisturizer is also available and refilled when needed.

The variety in the breakfast is not so big, but you have a coffee machine with many options to choose from, a minibar with plenty of yogurt available, 4 to 5 types of fresh fruit juice, croissants, pain au chocolat, 2-3 types of bread, cold cuts, hazelnut spread, butter and fruits available. All is refilled before you can notice. 

The vibe of the hotel is very nice: modern (as its name says), vibrant, happy, exciting. 
The surroundings are very nice: you have a metro station a block away from the hotel (Maubert-Mutualité, from line 10), and while you walk from it to the hotel, you can spot the Panthéon at the end of the street - a very gorgeous view! Literally next to the hotel, there is a pizza place (Pizza Roma Écoles) with amazing authentic italian pizzas and pasta. Boulangeries and patisseries are also around, as well as bistros. A great, great plus is having a Franprix on the same block, which is no more than a 3-minute walk to.

All in all, my staying there was perfect! Staff is very friendly (props to Marie and the night guy, that I was not able to get the name, for being so nice to me) and ready to help with whatever you need. I will definitely stay there again, and recommend this hotel for anyone who wishes to have the most pleasant stay in Paris!

title: Great location
text:
I have been to many hotels in Paris (see my other reviews over the years), so I have a pretty reasonable understanding of what to expect.  The location is outstanding. I have previously stayed in this area---right next door at the Hotel Saint Jacques, in fact.  This was my first stay at this hotel.
I booked this hotel for my sister and myself (two single rooms) on Expedia with breakfast included.
We arrived very early in the day so our rooms were not ready. We went out and about while the hotel locked our luggage in a secure room.
Upon return at around 3pm, our rooms were ready. The staff were very pleasant. When I went into my room, it was fine. Nothing spectacular, nothing ornate. The room was very basic--a bed, a closet with shelves, and a desk with a chair. It was not huge, but it was comfortable for one person. There were nice, large French doors that opened onto the rue des Ecoles below.  I enjoyed opening the windows to hear and see Paris!

The Bathroom
There is no actual door to the bathroom, just a very heavy curtain. This was fine as I was in my room alone and privacy was not an issue. I do have to say, that my only concern was in the bathroom. I am a relatively small person (5'5" and not overweight) and the shower was SMALL.  I could not shave my legs because I could not lift my leg and shave it--and I could not bend entirely over to reach my leg without my head hitting the wall. When washing my hair, I had to keep my elbows somewhat down or they hit the walls of the shower. If my husband or sons had been on this trip and needed to use this type of shower, it would have been impossible as they are tall with athletic builds (6'4" and muscular)--they would not have fit in the shower. It worked okay for me, but it was tight.
I had only one complaint, which I voiced to the reception personnel. There was a significant amount of black mold in my shower. I asked the personnel on day 1 if they could put some bleach or something on the mold to remove it. I am sensitive to mold, and it is just not safe especially in a very small shower and being fueled by hot shower water.  The mold was never addressed,and I just tried to take a very fast shower to avoid inhaling any potentially airborne mold.
Breakfast
The breakfast area was pleasant and the food was a very typical French fare. I was a bit disappointed that there were no actual baguettes there, instead rolls and other breads.  There were croissants, fruit, yogurt, deli meats and wonderful cheese.  The coffee machine was great as well.
The Lobby
The lobby area is a bit small, but it serves its purpose. There is hot tea, coffee and some small croissants and pain au chocolat available in the afternoon, which was a nice touch.

Overall, it was a fine stay, but if I go back to this area, I would probably not stay at this hotel again. The area is great though--very safe, even at night. The hotel location is really wonderful and the staff were very pleasant.

Anyway, I liked  the location and the staff but was disappointed with these 2 things.

Also atypical for Paris there is a fridge and coffee/tea making facilities so we bring our own fresh milk and preferred tea bags etc so we can have breakfast biscuits and drinks in the room and save €25 or so each day. Breakfast in the hotel is OK but simple.

Last week the douaniers decided to work to rule at Gard du Nord specifically disrupting outgoing Eurostar and on the Thursday we were texted a message advising us not to travel the following day. So we were a bit stuck.

After a bit of research on the net we found the only sensible route home was to fly but nothing was available until the Saturday.

I went and spoke to the lady on reception who initially said they had no availability for the Friday night but offered to consult their sister hotel after a bit of discussion with her colleague she closed the call. And after a bit of keyboard work and clarification she said she had rearranged a few room allocations and freed up our existing room for the additional night. For which I was very grateful indeed - also the room rate was sensible - no attempt to rip off. So we were then able to book two of the last few remaining seats on the BA flight on the Saturday afternoon and relax and enjoy an extra day in the sunshine in Paris.

Thank you Hotel M - we will be back!!

title: Great spot near
text:
This is a great little boutique hotel on Rue de Ecoles. The University of Paris (Sorbonne) is about a block away. And the Notre Dame cathedral is less than a 10-minute walk. There are great dining and shopping options within minutes as well as the Pantheon up a hill just behind the hotel that has a pretty great nighttime view of the Eiffel Tower.

Rooms are not chain hotel standard, my sisters and I each had a single room and none of them were the same. Some items were standard, a small fridge, a wall-mounted television, and a small desk. My room was orange-ish, my sister on the fourth floor had a purple-ish room, and my sister on the third floor had a blue-ish room. Each of us had a small Juliet balcony that overlooked the street below. I took advantage of my fifth floor location and stood outside several times each day. I couldn't see much over the buildings nearby but they view was a terrific city scene.

One complaint, literally one, was there were not enough outlets in my room, I had to unplug either the fridge or the tea kettle to get a plug for my phone and table. But my sisters had plugs right next to their beds. Kind of a pain, but the plugs were easy to get to. 

The staff was excellent, don't worry if your French is rusty or non-existent, they all speak English quite well and are super helpful. If you need to check in a bit early they can be accommodating, we arrived around noon and were allowed to check-in then. They can also arrange for transportation to the airport, about 90 euros for a van to CDG, which was about 30 euros less than we paid from the airport.

This was a terrific location, convenient to a lot of stuff and we loved it. They have wi-fi, a cute little lounge, and a nice breakfast area. HIGHLY recommended if you want something with a bit of character.

title: Super Strategic Location close to Gare de l'Est, Bus stop & Metro
text:
When I arrived that day I got stuck because no metro runs to Gare de l'Est hikkss...but with all of my euphoria on my holiday in Paris, I can escape from the stuck and the stranded at Chatelet Metro station (getting down from metro line 14 who runs without driver). Luckily it is easy to find Police around, I asked the way to go to Gare de l'Est and in fact it's very very easy just turn right and walk straight along the main street until end. Thanks God that the Libertel Gare de l'Est Hotel just few meters after the BK, wow very near and easy to find. 

First when I arrived at the hotel, I feel so tired but the receptionist, Mr. Shamim, is really kind, welcome and helpful. And because after got a hard time by the metro strike I suddenly feel safe in this hotel and comfortable too, finally arrived. Thus shortly, the location for me is super strategic! the bus stop and the metro station is just few meters away, also the Asian restaurant just across the street, BK and McD just around the corner, the supermarket just next door, pharmacy just across the street, many eateries around contained local food, middle east food, etc, a lot! also the international train station Gare de l'Est is just across the street! Perfect location for me. Bus number 32 could carry you to Eifel Tower and you can even walking until Notredame and river seine, to Leningrad also. Montmatre, Moulin Rouge also only took the bus in the bus stop nearby the Hotel doorstep. I'm lucky to stay in Libertel because of Metro strike and the hotel location is super, fit in with my needs. The bus (though full) still running, thus no worries about the metro strike. You even can walk to Galeries Lafayette, Opera Building, Hard Rock Cafe from the hotel, used Moovit apps to help you find the way. 

Back to the hotel review, the room is nice not too big but we still have space! I have no complaints and I like got the room facing to the street so I can look the situation over the window, there is a kettle with coffee/tea, bathroom amenities is also provided. Breakfast is also nice and have some variety and at least there is a hot stuff on the buffet as outside was cold brrr...well, it's enough for our stomach until lunch for sure! Wifi is also good no worries

Mr. Shamim, the receptionist help us to call a taxi to Paris Bercy Seine station and it's not too far just about 4,5km from the hotel which is good we don't deal with the traffic and time constraint, etc. 

Well, I definitely will stay here again if I back to Paris next time but hope no more metro strike please.....Merci beacoup Libertel Gare de l'Est

title: Great Location, Super Service & Excellent Value
text:
I stayed here prior to taking a train from Gare de l'Est to Strasbourg. Gare de l'est is literally steps away from this hotel.   So I went there the night before my departure to see what the layout and procedure for boarding was and also used the convenient ATM and small but good grocery store there (there are various shops and cafes there too).  When I first arrived to the hotel I was about 2 hours early before check in and was really tired because I had taken an overnight flight from the US, got a ride to the Opera area from the airport (dropped some luggage at another location there), and walked 20+ blocks to the Libertel hotel.  When I arrived the front desk staff "Shamim" made me feel welcome, showed me where I could temporarily store my lugage and offered that I could wait in there very comfortable waiting area near the dinning.  He got me into my room earlier than regular check-in and I was very relieved and grateful. Later that evening another staff member happily chatted with me and really god restaurant with the type of cuisine I was looking for. The following day Shamim, on duty again, alerted me to some cancelled trains to Germany and advised I check mine to Strasbourg. If mine was cancelled he could help me quickly book another night there. Fortunately, my train was not cancelled, I just had to wait a couple of hours after check-out for it. He invited me to wait again in the comfortable waiting areas where her offered me beverages and made me feel comfortable.  When one is on travel, and esp alone, it is always nice and very helpful to have such warm, thoughtful and professional staff. I really appreciated this. The facilities and room are very clean and up-to-date.  A bit small as it is in many major metro cities (like NYC) it was fine for me, had everything I needed and was comfortable. To be honest you can hear the subway trains underground. I lived in NYC for many years and know this is a not unusual in any city with an extensive subway system. So I recommend asking for upper floors and the quiter rooms but also if you bring a pair of ear plugs that may be good enough.
Overall this hotel is an excellent value and ultra convenient if you need to take a train from Gare de lEst and its not that far from Gare du Nord also.

title: Very pleasant stay
text: My daughter and I spent 1 night here on the recommendation of a friend. We were not disappointed. The hotel is situated less than 10 mins walk from Gard Du Nord Station, although our phone map sent us on the wrong route on arrival and we found ourselves in a not too desirable area. We didn't make this mistake on our return trip, that said there are many quite intimidating characters that hang around Gard Du Nord trying to sell cigarettes etc. We simply ignored them, I don't think we'd have done the journey after dark. The hotel is lovely and simple and perfect for a mini break. Reception is clean, smart and inviting. We arrived around 11;30am and were advised our room would be ready at 2pm so we placed our bags in the luggage room and set off for the Metro to start our tour of Paris. Turning right outside the hotel a short distance along is one of the Gard De L'Est Metro entrances. On arrival in the ticket hall we were approached by someone asking if we required help, we declined. We joined the queue for our tickets and another helper appeared. Now these people wear lanyards with some sort of ID pass attached but plain clothes so 1st impressions you think they're employed by the Transport Company. It became apparent when she insisted on helping us and claiming that the machines only accepted French credit cards that this was a scam. She said the 2 day Metro pass for 2 persons was 79.95 Euros and as we didn't have a French CC, we'd have to pay cash. We told her we didn't have cash and left, but not before 2 young French girls asked if they'd offered to help, we said Yes, they told us NO do not deal them. On reading reviews online it would appear this is rife all over the Paris Metro. So please be aware! Anyway back to the hotel, we returned around 5pm and got our key. The room is perfect for a mini break. Very clean and compact. Bed was extremely comfortable with 2 pillows each. There is adequate clothes hanging space for a few days stay. A free safe is provided along with tea and coffee making facilities. A stocked mini bar too. TV with mainly French channels but we found a music channel. Bathroom is lovely, great shower, shower gel and soap if you needed it and clean white towels. Hotel was quiet at night, that said you can hear the rumble of the Metro below the hotel but its not enough to disturb sleep and Metro is closed by around 2AM. Overall for what we paid, it was excellent value and a great base for exploring Paris and the return trip via Eurostar. We were room only but there was an option to upgrade to B&B on arrival. The reception staff we found friendly and helpful. I would recommend this hotel for a mini break and I would definitely return should I visit Paris again

title: Nope. Not for me. Too many issues.
text:
Recommendation: I would only recommend this hotel if, (1) your are coming late and leaving early because your main priority is something close to Paris Gare de l'Est station, and (2) you live in a big city and are used to or not bothered by lots of noise. 

Room: I paid for the bigger room supposedly for two. When I walked in I figured they must have made a mistake and given me the small room for one. But no, this was the big room. I don't want to know how small the small room was! That said it was clean, the bed was fine, the bathroom large and had a very nice soaking tub. 
    Not so good stuff. Broken AC/Heather. I couldn't even get the fan to come on. They offered to move me to a different room, but it would have been closer to the street and even more noisy than this one. Speaking of that, I checked twice to see if the window was open because there was *no* sound barrier from the street. But no, it was closed just the worst sound insulation ever. The wifi worked but was slow. 

Location: What a horrible part of the city. I booked this place because I was coming in late to Paris du Nord, and I really didn't want to get lost late at night. The website said it was ) 0.1 miles away from the station. Well it was a mistake as it is very close to the  l'EST station but not du Nord. So I spent an hour trying to find it. This was literally the dirtiest neighborhood I've ever seen in my life. Trash, broken beer bottles, teenagers peeing in the street, oddly random pieces of dirty underwear on the street (yes!) and homeless person excrement everywhere. There is a lot of homeless people, random people trying to sell you cigarettes, and no grass for dogs. 
      I thought it was odd that Paris is supposed to be a dog friendly city and the only two parks I could find did not allow dogs. I've never even heard of public parks that do not allow dogs. All the plants in the city are fenced off, perhaps because if they weren't they would quickly be destroyed. There is lots of restaurants, most look like fast food. If you are standing facing the hotel I recommend heading left instead of right if you are walking around (but women shouldn't do this alone at night). Left is still bad but better than right. This place is far from the Eiffel tower.

Noise level: just awful. The window provides absolutely no sound isolation. For reasons I can't understand there is constant honking, street racing, and random screaming. You should definitely try to get a room away from the street, but I am suspect it would be quiet, and if you are at all sensitive do not consider staying here unless a non-street side room is guaranteed.  

Amenities: expensive breakfast (much better off going to a close bakery), very tiny lifts (elevators), dog friendly for an incredibly high fee, 30 euros a night, which is more than listed on their webpage (25), With two dogs that could be more than the price of the room. I don't think anything else here could be called an amenity. 

Service: Not friendly. Only one person works at night so if there is a problem they can't really help, as they have to stay downstairs. At least when I was there, there was not anyone to help with bags. 

Value: I paid 100 euros, plus dog fee. So many better places for less.

title: 5 star rating hotel
text:
I am very happy that I chose this hotel, I was traveling with my mother who is 80, and my daughter who is 14, so this trip was supposed to be memorable, we were coming here after spending some time in London.
It is a very wonderful hotel with a very professional and understanding staff.
I really liked how the company transformed an old building into a 5 star rating hotel.
The inside is super modern and spacious. There is a big reception where you have the choice of sitting down and reading their wide variety of brochures about Paris and its surroundings or you can enjoy their free wifi while sitting on a very comfortable couch.
The receptionists are very kind and welcoming. When you have a problem, they will do their best to find a solution.
When we arrived it was pretty late, we were given a room on the second floor.
On the second floor and on almost all of the floors you can hear the metro zooming underground, so the building shakes and you really can't have some peace and quiet.
Our room was 201, next to the elevator. The inside of the room was an okay size for three people staying 9 nights and it was very clean. The bathroom was pretty small. The view was not what we expected to see for 9 nights, in gorgeous Paris. The view was of the interior "garden". The kitchen vent where all of the smell and heat came was right next to our noses. When you looked out the window you just saw walls on the left,right and in front of you. Plus, the sun didn't reach the room at all. We were disappointed because we have read very excellent reviews about this hotel and this is what they gave us? Especially that we were staying 9 nights here.
After spending a night here, I could not even sleep, the next morning I went to the lobby and told the receptionist that this room is not what we wanted nor what we expected. The receptionist was very nice and patient and she called her manager so we can work things out. In the end, the wonderful, beautiful, understanding manager gave us an amazing room. She went over the top to find us a better room. She was very, very nice.
We got are luggages and went to the new room, which was on the fifth floor. When we saw the room we were speechless.
It was a good sized room because it was usually a 2 person room, but since we have a third person with us they brought a foldable bed. The room had lots of drawers to put your necessities. The bathroom was huge. A giant tub with a good mirror and a nice sink. Our favorite part of the room was the balcony! The room had a huge balcony in the main sleeping area and the bathroom! The balcony is narrow so you do have to be careful when you're outside. When you looked outside you saw the Gare De L' Est and the street that the hotel is situated on.
Anyway this room is beyond what we expected, you can make you tea or coffee, you have e fridge, and it is very very clean.
The hotel has a super good placement. You are less than a hundred meters from the Gare. Next to the hotel is the supermarket Monoprix, with a wild variety of food and drinks.
A fifteen minute walk to Montmartre if you want to see that area. Just walk up the Boulevard Magenta to get to Montmartre.
Less than a ten minute walk to Place de la Republique, where there are lots of good restaurants.
Overall this is an amazing hotel that I will definitely return to in the future next time that I visit Paris. 
5 star rating all the way!

I had also arrived from the US in Paris 3 weeks earlier and looking back I wish I'd chosen this place instead of the one I did (no reason to name it) at the beginning of my trip as well. I usually stay near rail stations when I visit Europe, and often it is very difficult to find a really nice place near one. You can see this hotel as soon as you walk out of the Gare de l'Est (if you know in which direction to look) and it is nicer than others in that area or near the Gare du Nord that I have stayed at. I highly recommend it, for the reasonable price and the nice clean facilities, as well as its helpful staff.

I would add that when I contacted the hotel a few days before my check-in date to tell them that I would be arriving between 10:30-11 am (an hour usually far too early at which to check in) they wrote back and offered me an early check-in for 30 Euros. I instantly took them up on it - their prices are so good that my total even with early check-in was approx 100 Euros - an unusual offer, and very much appreciated

title: HIDDEN BUGS & FEES
text: If you don’t look close enough, this hotel appears to be decent, good even. Perfect location, clean room, seemingly friendly receptionist, until you look a little closer. When you do, small flies appear in the bathroom and on the table, You find there is no shower gel or toilet paper in the bathroom. The TV doesn’t work, and isn’t fixed, even after you bring it to their attention. And a surprise city tax (hey, €11.55 in cash, on top of an overpriced, bug-infested room, when not expected, added insult to injury) is presented to you at check-out. I should have seen the sign from the way they handled a change in my reservation. After being notified by Air France of a upcoming strike, I booked a room a night earlier than expected, but the hotel would not refund the €30 surcharge I initially paid for an early arrival. Despite the fact that this was way beyond my control. No understanding, no flexibility. Yet, they expect understanding about the less than adequate conditions, or maybe they don’t care? When checking-out of the hotel and surprised with the city tax, I questioned why this wasn’t mentioned anywhere, and the receptionist replied rudely, and a heated discussion ensued - not what you want before a long trip home. The hotel’s attitude towards these issues, and general laissez-faire, “too bad”, response was not desirable nor helpful, and far from service-minded. In short, not a good experience. It’s a shame, because it has all the right ingredients, but the wrong attitude. I hope someone from Libertel Gare de l’Est reads this and cleans up their act. And that you, lovely people reading this, get a fair warning.

title: I loved listening to music blasting when I was trying to sleep and stepping in water when using the toilet
text: Look, the location is nice because it's right by the gare du nord station and that's the extent of the positives for me. When we checked in, they informed us we would be receiving free breakfast in exchange for a positive review, well jokes on you because you're not getting one, I will not be bribed! I don't like when a company offers you something for free so you can give a good review. You bet I ate free breakfast though. However, I was in Paris, I should have been having an actual good meal so whatever, at least I saved money. Anyways, onto the hostel. Here's the thing, the hostel surrounds a restaurant/bar/club. This is good when you want to eat at the hostel, this is bad when it's 2 AM on the weekend and you want to sleep but can't because the music is blasting and the bass is thumping in your chest. I couldn't believe someone designed a space where people are supposed to sleep directly above a loud club. If it was next door I would have understood, but no, it is attached to the hostel. I also came back at around 7 pm the next day thinking I could rest a bit, but nope, the music was there then too. The other thing I hated was the flooded bathrooms. I take a shower and the drain is clogged so the water starts flooding into the bathroom itself. You go into a stall and there's a puddle of water by your feet, how did that even get there? And it happened in both bathrooms near my room. They have floor squeegees in the bathroom. The room itself was fine. Had curtains in the bunks and a sink plus a table but the flooded bathrooms and loud music on the weekends all night made me dislike my stay. I will say the staff was very nice and they did have events for guests but you're still getting a negative review. Thanks for the free breakfast though!

title: Low Price, Lower Value
text:
When I looked into booking a 3-night stay in Paris, I was already familiar with many hostels across Europe. However, I didn't manage to stay in St. Christopher's hostel until my Parisian visit. I didn't know anyone who stayed there in the past to advise, So I booked my place based on online reviews.

Unfortunately, I'm taking the time to write a detailed review, so other people that plan to stay at St Christopher's Gare du Nord would have the entire picture, before investing their time and money by booking a room or a bed there.

Despite the fact that the hostel offer quite cheap offer relatively hotels in the area, I think that at the end of the day the final package that you get doesn't work the discount in price. For example, my experience in Jo&Joe (also a Parisian hostel) was significantly better, and the difference in price was 2-3 euros a night. 
St. Christopher's provides a defective product

Problems:

the rooms:
the rooms were not clean. After going back from the shower to the room, I kept having the feeling I need to take a shower again. The curtains of the bed looked like there were not being cleaned for at least six months.
When it comes to power sockets, I stayed in a 4 beds room, and there were barely 2 sockets for all of us in the entire room. Why would you save money on something basic like that?  
There was a lack of basic things that really impacted the convenience - another example is the lack of personal lamps, a basic thing you should have when sharing a room with other people. I had to use my camera's flashlight every time in order to not wake up my roommates.

Breakfast: Despite investing a lot in marketing their breakfast, the one that I received in St. Christopher's was the worst I have had, out of all of my trips around the world. As someone who served in the military and used to eat low-quality food, trust me that I'm not exaggerating. There was a very hard baguette, Pastrami, the most simple cheese, yogurt in a huge bowl and fruit salad. that's it. there wasn't even water (!) or cups for coffee. Had to drink coffee from a beer cup...

Showers: I think it's mind-boggling to have 2 showers and 2 toilets in a floor that hosts tens of people, not only that every time I had to go to the bathroom and shower there was usually a line there, but also then all of the facilities become very dirty in a very short period of time. And, they were not being cleaned frequently enough. 

To summarize, for me it was a bad experience. There are many other great hostels in Paris and in general that are delivering a great experience at an affordable price, but St Christopher's Gare du Nord fails to deliver the most basic things that travelers need.

Therefore, I recommend staying away from St Christopher's, and finding an alternative for your stay in Paris.
