title: It’s tight but it’s Paris
text: This  is my second stay at the Paris France Hotel. This time I brought the family. We were heading home from Prague and took 3 nights in Paris to explore. I love the location of this hotel. It is super close to 2 good metro stops. It is next to a beautiful church and close to so many places to eat and buy food.  We stayed in a room that sleeps four. Here’s my beef: The double bed was a pull out couch and not a great one. It left us with just about a foot to get to the spacious and so lovely bathroom. I would have rather not have slept on a sofa bed.  That is my only complaint. The desk help is lovely and kind. The hotel is old but well kept and our room was clean and cared for each day. It is a good value a great location.  I plan to return the next time I am in Paris.

title: Simple, clean and centrally located.
text: I found this hotel to be lovely. It's centrally located in the 3rd District, right next to a Metro station, and the rooms are simple, very clean, and the staff is quite accommodating. We did not want to spend all of our traveling money on an expensive hotel, and thus took a chance in booking this hotel based on reviews. We had a room on the 6th floor, and it faced the church, which provided a lot of privacy. We could see the Eiffel Tower from our room and at night enjoyed the light show. It was helpful to have an elevator, though small as it is. We did not pay for the breakfast package but ate downstairs one time, and the set-up is straightforward (cereal, toast, fruit, yogurt, croissants, coffee). We would stay here again.

title: 2nd time and Just as good
text: Have just stayed 3 nights at the Paris France Hotel. This was the 2nd time we have stayed there, and it was just as good this time as it was the 1st. The staff are helpful and friendly. The breakfast was perfect for us (lots of Coffee, Toast and croissants) the member of staff working in the Breakfast area was always cheerful and helpful. Our room was perfect for the 3 of us. Superb Pizza place just down the road, Metro to Gare Du Nord walking distance. The member of Nightstaff was very helpful when we tripped the fuses in our room. He promptly reset the fuses and gave us a much better travel plug than what we had with us. Will def visit again and again.

title: A Parisian charmer
text: It's funny how things I would not want in an American hotel (ie. older, mismatched furniture, slightly worn around the edges) are all part of the charm in a small European hotel. And this hotel has charm to spare! From the small lift to the view of a distant Eiffel Tower, we loved it here! The desk staff was friendly and helpful. The breakfast was adequate, though you might do better on your own. Bathroom was clean and modern. We found it well worth it to spend a little more on a larger room that had windows on two sides with wonderful views of the cafes, the church steeple next door and, as I said, the Eiffel Tower. Location was very near two metro stops and close to restaurants and  cafes (dine at Norma's just down the block for chic Italian. Full of locals, not tourists). If you prefer old world Parisian charm over slick, modern conveniences, check out the Paris France.

The location was such that I could walk to Notre Dame and also walked to the fabulous Lumier museum.  The neighborhood is amazing with good choices for eating.  I didn't see any continental breakfast as advertised.  But there are so many places to get food- who cares.  The front desk help spoke clear English and let me butcher French for practice.  They were France's version of friendly and that is exactly what I hoped for.  The bed was fine and the front desk called me a cab.  Absolutely a bargain. and If I ever get back to Paris, I will stay here again.  May it be so!

title: Great value
text:
There's everything to like about Hotel Paris France. The location is great - very close to the Republic metro station with connections to most lines and on the edge of the Marais district.  It is within walking distance of the city centre but far enough to be away from the very touristy parts. There are lots of cafes bars and restaurants nearby.
The hotel is comfortable without being flashy, and the proprietor is quietly friendly and helpful.
We had a room facing the street and with a small balcony. The room was quite plain, but perfectly comfortable and quite spacious for this type of hotel in Paris. The big surprise was the bathroom which was obviously new. It was spotlessly clean, very large and the best bit, had a proper shower (not a hand-held 'telephone' affair). 
Breakfast is served in the basement and while it is perfectly OK, you may find that you get better value by eating at one of the nearby cafes.
All in all a great little hotel and really good value for money. We will certainly return.

title: Great boutique hotel
text:
Stayed at this boutique hotel 10 nights. Excellent location - 1 min walk to Temple metro station and 3 min walk to République metro station from where you can transfer between other Metro lines. Only 3 stops from Gare du Nord station where you can catch a train to Charles de Gaulle airport. Monoprix supermarket with bakery (patisserie/boulangerie) section is behind the hotel. Very clean room #20  on the second floor with modern bathroom and lovely balcony facing main street. Small elevator that fits one person plus luggage or 2 people without luggage worked the whole 10 days I was there. All the staff there are helpful, especially English speaking Christelle. Most major attractions are a 20-30 minute stroll away.

Minor downsides: Small room size; In-room TV has only a couple of English speaking channels: BBC News and a couple of America business news channels  (but only a minor con as most people spend very little time in the room anyway when you're in Paris!)

I would definitely recommend this hotel and would stay here again.

My only complaint was the elevator which was in need of repair and did not go to the 7th floor so I would have to take the elevator to the sixth floor and walk up one flight.  That was no problem. Fortunately, this happened on the day of my departure and the concierge had to walk up six flights of stairs to get my luggage.  

I would recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a clean, safe, quiet, budget hotel!

title: Don't look for anything else in Paris
text: My son and I stayed here for several days and we couldn't have enjoyed our stay any more. We are very familiar with Paris hotels and also short term apartments over the years.  This was by far one of the best places and most reasonably priced hotels we've ever stayed at. The location of the hotel in the upper Marais and close to the Republique plaza is very sought after. With a very good location, the hotel is within a 3 minute walk from the Republique metro station and taxi stops (one of Paris' large plazas). It is also situated right next to a smaller metro stop, Temple. Easy walk from the hotel through the Marais, and all that it has to offer (parks, shops, bakeries, restaurants). Not only is it very accessible to public transportation, there are also several restaurants right next door or on the back of the hotel.  There is a Monoprix store (groceries, bakery, and other goods) right next door.  The rooms were remodeled, clean, with nicely refurbished bathrooms.  Our room, even though not huge, had a little porch with a view of the Eiffel Tower all the way at the other end of Paris.  The bathroom was very updated with granite and glass and steel and brand new fixtures, and huge in size compared to European standards.  I have been recommending this hotel to every one of my friends. Unless you want to rent a short term apartment, or stay at a very fancy hotel, or be close to the western part of Paris, this hotel offers you everything you need for an enjoyable stay with very reasonable room rates, plus more. I can't say enough about it. I am looking forward to my next trip.

title: Overall enjoyable stay
text:
Pros:

1. Hotel environment and rooms are modern and clean
2. Location is only a short walk to the Eiffel Tower and has great views
3. Hotel is in a good location with many conveniences close by (ex. grocery store, laundromat, bank, bakeries, restaurants, etc.).
4. All of the hotel staff were very helpful and cheerful

Cons:

1. Room service menu and breakfast were mediocre
2. Regarding water, they give you a glass bottle and you have to fill it up yourself via filtered water dispenser on the ground floor. It's not a major inconvenience, but it's worth noting.
3. In our rooms, the toilet is in a separate room from the rest of the restroom. From what I've read, this is more of a France thing, and not just specific to this hotel. It's weird if you're not used to it.

Overall, the pros outweigh the cons, and getting a hotel in the Trocadero area can be pricy, so I'd say this is one of the better options overall.

title: GREAT ACCESS TO PARIS FOR FAMILIES
text: This hotel is in an excellent location for family access to Paris.  Arrival was seamless after a long flight and with views of the Eiffel Tower out there front door.  The Trocadero area is quiet and quaint yet w/ a Metro stop 2-3 min walk away you have super easy access to the whole city.  The Canopy staff is very welcoming and almost all spoke very good English if important to you.  We were welcomed and recognized as Diamond members upon check-in.  We were in a connected King Family Suite with a Twin Double Room.  The kids (3) took the King Suite as it had a King and pull out sofa.  We were on Floor 5 (of 6 room floors).  View of the top of the tower was nice (to help with the feel of being in Paris for the kids but not extravagant).  However, the 7th floor rooftop terrace has a PHENOMENAL view of the Tower.  NOTE: the 7th floor gets crowded and not seemingly  as kid  friendly although we could not get a table and chose to retire.  Service was excellent.  Breakfast and breakfast service was excellent.  HIGHLY RECOMMEND this hotel for a boutique feel and very accessible yet somewhat off the beaten path.  Only one minor nitpick and that is the bathrooms were small and the WC was separated from the shower area but this is due to efficient room layout so it does not change our opinion of the hotel at all…just pointing it out…great stay in Paris.

title: Lousy Service Overall. Not a Hilton Experience!!!
text:
Lousy Service Overall. Not a Hilton at all. When you book a Hilton Hotel you expect Hilton Service, it is not the case here. You do not have 24 hour service. Should you need something after 9-10 pm (i.e., soap, ice,  towels etc.) you have to come down to the lobby yourself and wish they have enough. Room service (food) is very limited and not 24 hours. The roof top (bar?restaurant) has a great view but a lousy service; we stayed at the hotel for 6 nights and were never able to have the steak (seems they have only 4 pieces for a more than 100 hundred guests hotel.  Two nights they even didnt had coke zero (told us there was a shortage, but except for here in all other places you could find it. We once ordered a cesars salad for room service and it was awful (no cheese etc); our overall opinion of the roof top is that all they want is to finish their day (and limited food there) quickly so that they can go home.

We book a cab in the hotel for the airport with 2 days in advance for the day we were living (we specifically told them a van or big car as we were a big party with plenty luggage)….they told us everything was booked and then they only could get us a small cab…had to run to the street and found one ourselves.

On our last morning we hadnt made the checkout and they were already “cleaning” our room, but all other days they made it from 4 to 5 pm….we couldnt use it anymore. Fyi…it seems they dont clean the rooms they only make your beds.

Overall we were expecting the Hilton service but we didnt had it…….

title: Mixed bag -check in poor- breakfast great- rooftop bar not worth wait.
text:
Arrived early (10a) they held out bags as rooms weren’t ready.  We went out for the day and returned about 7p. A nice man checked us in however he didn’t give us any information.  I went back down to ask about Diamond member breakfast perks ect.  He said he assumed the women in the morning had told us which she hadn’t.  My Diamond status wasn’t recognized and having used 80k points per night I was a touch surprised by this.  After freshening up in the room we found no shampoo or bar soap.  Called desk they said the hotel was completely out of soap waiting on a shipment?  Found this cheap as soap is sold on every corner of Paris.  They brought shampoo and body gel.  

The highlight was breakfast-great greeter and servers both mornings. 

Rooftop bar- we had better experience at the hotel Raphael rooftop bar-same view.  The Service was so slow from moment we sat down it took 40 minutes to get our drinks with no apology.  

I would like at least 40k of my 160k points back for the issues.

title: Awesome boutique hotel in a convenient location
text:
TLDR: Perfect boutique hotel in a great location in Paris. Breakfast is to die for, do not miss it!

Pros:
1. Location: it’s a 5-10 min walk to Eiffel Tower! And you can even see the tower from the hotel rooftop!
2. Design: the hotel has a great design. Reminds me of the design hotels of Marriott. From the lobby, on-site restaurant, to the room, you can tell they have very design details taken care of 
3. Breakfast: we got free breakfast as a diamond member and it was not your typical hotel breakfast. It’s a full serviced breakfast with staff taking your order with a la cart menu, and they would also bring out specialties for you to try throughout the breakfast service. My favorite is the detox ginger shot and hot cheese and ham croissant. There is also a small buffet section you can get bread, pastries and scrambled eggs if you want. The breakfast is the highlight of my stay!
4. Gym: decent gym with free weights, treadmills, and a couple machines. Again the hotel is so new so the gym is spanking new too, you can get a good workout in here for sure.

Cons:
Not much really, but if I have to be super picky, here are two:
1. Room size: we got upgraded to premium king from regular king room and it still felt a bit small. But I guess that is the norm for Parisian hotels in the city center. 
2. Fish and chips: we ordered fish and chips from the hotel restaurant. It was their take on fish and chips where you really got chips as Americans would say (or for British it crisps). And the fish is fried fish paste formed strip. It was good but probably the British will think it’s blasphemy.

title: Fantastic Stay at this Gem of a Hotel in the Heart of the Trocadero
text:
Long-time Hilton Diamond member, first-time reviewer.

My partner and I recently stayed at the new Canopy hotel in the Trocadero.  We love the neighborhood and typically stay at a competitor hotel, but as it had been nearly two years since our last Paris visit, we decided to change things up.

We couldn't have been more pleased with the experience and have adopted this hotel as our new home in Paris for future stays.

First, the hotel is brand-new, clean, and hip.  The view from the front door is a majestic vista of the Eiffel Tower bookmarked by two blocks of gorgeous Trocadero apartments. Second, the staff are incredibly welcoming and go above and beyond to make you feel comfortable.  From the early check-in to drinks on the roof and the delicious breakfast every morning, we felt right at home and (as we were staying for a week) felt like we knew all the staff by face, if not by name, by the end of our stay.

The bedrooms are well-appointed, and the gym is one of the nicest I've ever used at a hotel, Hilton or otherwise.

My only two cons - our room, a premier king room, could have benefited with a better occasional chair.  Rather than a comfy lounger, there was essentially a padded office chair in the corner.  Also, the beautiful bathroom has an attractive, translucent wall panel.  It is only until the middle of the night that you realize it completely lights up the bedroom if someone conducts any nighttime ablutions. (This may have just been our room, however.)

All in all, coming back to Paris during Covid was a bit of a trial, but we couldn't have been happier with the trip, in no small part due to our experience at this wonderful hotel.

text:
The hotel is brand new, with an exciting interior design paying hommage to the French art deco of the 1930s.  It is located in a very nice and upscale residential neibourhgood, just around the corner from a metro station.  The rooms are not very big, but creatively and efficiently designed, and some offer a partial view of the Eiffel Tower.  For the full view of the tower make sure to book a table at the terrace and enjoy a cocktail or a dinner there.  The best thing about the hotel, however, is its outsanding team.  Every employee was very welcoming and professional, but I would particularly like to mention four team members with whom we interacted the most:

The Chief Enthusiast (hotel manager) Ms. Lorent was very helpful in allaying my concerns about this brand-new property which lacked customer reviews when I wanted to book it, and assuring me that everything will be in order by the time we arrive - which was certainly the case.  She also took the time from her busy schedule to speak to me and my family a number of times during our stay and and told us about the history of the hotel, answered our questions, etc.

The Lead Welcome Enthusiast (head consierge) Ms. Ester Barrios-Arshak has been incredibly responsive and attentive to our needs.  She changed our reservation dates when we had to postpone our trip due to the continued COVID restrictions while securing the approval to keep our original room rates; she upgraded us upon check-in; and after learning about my daughter's love of baking she even proposed to organize a private baking class for her with the hotel's chef Mr. Kubarek.  She also provided us with useful information on sightseeing, and checked on our request whether certain museums were open, etc.  In short, she made our stay simply unforgettable!

The Lead Kitchenb Enthusiast (heda chef) Mr. Robin Kubarek cooked outstanding meals (we really enjoyed our a-la-carte breakfasts!) in a sparkling clean kitchen, and we could watch him at work through the window in the restaurant which was an excellent way of showcasing both his and his colleagues' skills and the top hygienic standards of the restaurant.  He also took the time for a private baking lesson for our daughter and introduced her to the secrets of French patisserie.  She absolutely loved the lesson and the unexpected presents she received from Mr. Kubarek - not just the cookies she baked, but also a personalized recipe book, a jar with baking mix and even a personalized chef's hat!  This was a truly unforgettable experience for her and for us. 

Finally the (head?) waiter Thibault provided us with outstanding service during our stay.  In addition to attending to our every need during breakfast time, one evening he offered us a bartending demonstration mixing delicious cocktails (and a mocktail for our daughter) for the family.  He was always very upbeat, courteous and attentive to our every need.  France definitely need more service professionals like him!
description: Located in Paris’ 16th arrondissement, our hotel is in a prime location for sightseeing. We’re within two km. of the Arc de Triomphe, Eiffel Tower, Trocadero Gardens, Champs-Elysees, and Bois de Boulogne. Trocadero Metro Station is just 210 meters away. Our vibrant neighborhood hotel features a rooftop terrace and bar with views of the Eiffel Tower.

title: Excellent service, superb location
text: Warm and professional service team.  Lovely boutique hotel with finishes consistent with this status.  Location was perfect for us to be able to see Musee d' Orsay just minutes after we arrived.  Would definitely stay again.

title: Amazing beautiful Hotel
text:
I spent 2 nights at this beautiful hotel and it’s the only place I’ll stay in Paris when I go back.  The staff were so friendly, helpful and welcoming! 
Located on a charming little street close to the Tuileries, the Louvre , the Metro and many other sites . 
The Mayfair is an elegant Parisian style hotel , exactly what one might expect in Paris .  The rooms are stunning, the breakfast was delicious . I’m looking forward to my next trip to France which will include staying at this hotel. Many thanks to everyone at the Mayfair .

title: Amazing Hotel!    Great folks, comfortable and an excellent location!
text: LOVED IT FROM THE START TO THE FINISH!     Traveling with my daughters we had an incredible stay at the Mayfair.   We had been there before the Pandemic and were treated like old friends and family.  There are not enough nice things to say about them.  Comfortable without any problem,  perfect location for easy exploration and so charming that it was like staying with friends.   Not much of a view, but the ease of access made up for it.   Why worry about looking out a window when you are less then five minutes from the best of Paris.      GO THERE OFTEN!

title: Location
text:
My wife and I were at the Mayfair Paris hotel a few days ago.  We got room 61. What makes this hotel is the location, close to several of the key museums (Louvre, Musee d'Orsay, etc, etc.  The room is comfortable, clean. Bathroom is fine, but not very practical for people who take a shower every day (no curtains or glass doors to prevent the water from getting to the floor).
Breakfast was adequate, nothing to write home about it.
Please note, they advertise the hotel has having public parking available. In reality the hotel is located in a very narrow street, a real nightmare to get the rental car to the front of the hotel.  I had to leave the car at the Place de Vendome parking, which is about 3 blocks from the hotel.
Please note, we have been in France 9 times, therefore, have been exposed to other hotels.

title: Classical but modern hotel
text: We spent 3 nights in the Mayfair and enjoyed our stay immensely. Great location just a few minutes walk from the Tuileries gardens and Louvre. The hotel combines classical French style with modern conveniences.. The rooms were equipped with  several usb charging  points and a good Wi-Fi connection. All  the staff were friendly, courteous and very efficient.  Special mention for the lovely lady who ran the breakfast room.  Always a welcoming smile, and nothing was too much trouble! The hotel is highly recommended and hopefully we will have an opportunity to stay there again.

title: Broken Elevator
text: I recently stayed at the hotel, and yes it is  cute and a good location to shopping and museums. However,  some of the front desk staff didn't seem like they had it all together.. and unfortunately I stayed on the top floor, which is the 6th floor and the elevator broke for 3 days and going up and down 6 flights of stairs with no A/C in the hallway several times a day was exhausting and painful as I have bulginging disc's in my back and an injured knee which were aggravated deeply by the stair use and really held me back on sight seeing. I asked for a discount on our bill and the staff gave us the run around and although there  was nothing they can do about a broken elevator they could have at least treated me with a discount as a kind gesture. Many of the hotel guest felt the same way as I spoke to many. Even the Bellman was struggling. If a company as big as Iprefer can't extend a kind gesture then I will not be a loyal member anymore.

title: If you want to stay on the right bank between The Louvre and Rue St. Honore this the place.
text: Great location on a quiet street off of Rue de Rivoli. Rooms are spacious and we planned. No restaurant but room service is great for breakfast. Requests for ice were met in a matter of minutes. Second time staying there and would return.

title: Broken elevator no compensation
text: The elevator broke down over a 3 day portion of our stay. It was incredibly hot and we were on the 6th floor. Walking up and down 6 flights of stairs was a understandably a huge inconvenience. We asked for a discount on our bill and our request fell upon stunned and gazed eyes. We feel there should have been some kind of compensation for our dream of a lifetime trip. They said there was nothing they could do and it would be forwarded to the manager.  Still waiting to hear.

title: A Lovely May Stay at Hotel Mayfair
text: On recommendation of our travel adviser, we booked at Hotel Mayfair for four nights.  This boutique hotel is well located near Place de Concorde and across the street from the Jardin de Tuilerie.  The Louvre is about three blocks down the street.   Our room was lovely, clean and comfortable.  The staff was excellent as was the corner brasserie !  Don't believe the bad rap Parisians are given about rudeness.  They were gracious and helpful whenever we had questions.  We were also pleasantly surprised when our room was ready earlier than expected!  Thank you, Hotel Mayfair, for your excellent room and stay!  We will be back!

title: Small and Beautiful
text: Very small, very beautiful hotel that is close to everything.   Just steps from The Louvre and Tulleries Garden you can walk to Champs Elysées and beyond.  The staff are at the front desk 24 hrs and helpful with suggestions for dining or obtaining tickets.  There is a pretty little bar off of the small lobby where breakfast is offered daily.

title: Beautiful Hotel in a great location
text: Loved our stay at the Hotel Mayfair Paris. The Hotel is very beautiful and is in a great central location. Everyone at the hotel were  extremely nice and helpful. The breakfast was outstanding as well.

title: Paris Home away from Home
text: I have found my new home in Paris!! I loved my stay at the Hotel Mayfair. The staff were excellent. Personal service and detail. Before I arrived they arranged many restaurant bookings for me which I really appreciated. On arrival we were upgraded to a junior Suite for our first night from a superior, and to a superior from a confort the remaining 3 nights, which again was extremely appreciated. I highly recommend the junior suite which was on the 6th (top) floor and had a balcony with views across the rooftops to jardin de tuileries. The beds were super comfortable. The rooms were nicely renovated. There was an espresso coffee machine in every room. We had a situation where a family member had tested positive for Covid thé day before our arrival and I had to have an extra youth with us last minute.. thé hôtel were very accommodating in finding a solution to fit the extra guest which wasn’t easy as they were fully booked. What I liked most was the renovated rooms and the personal intimate feel to thé hôtel. All the staff were so lovely and professional and personable. I spent a long time researching to find the hôtel that ticked all my boxes in this location within a budget I could afford. The last time I was in Paris 10 years ago I stayed at the George V hôtel abd the time before that the Ritz, which are of course hard shoes to fill.. but I really enjoyed this hotel for its excellent location, and small personable experience and nicely renovated rooms. It was perfect. It’s a real gem!!! J’ai hâte de retourner chez Hôtel Mayfair !!

title: Four nights in Paris
text: Lovely staff. Comfortable property. Great location. We were able to walk almost everywhere but the Metro was also close by. Hotel called taxis for us as needed. All of the desk staff were very helpful and friendly. We had an enjoyable stay!

title: Short break
text: The Hotel Mayfair Paris is a lovely, traditional little hotel, with lovely and very helpful staff. It’s conveniently situated for visiting the Louvre, Musee d’Orsay and the Orangeries, all within walking distance through the Tuileries. I will definitely be staying there again later in the year having found a safe and pleasant place to stay.

title: Fantastic!
text: The staff were so friendly,  nothing was too much trouble, they made my stay seem less and was always at hand should I need. The room was very spacious and had a large balcony, the room was well equipped, very clean, the location was great! I cannot wait to go back.

title: An absolutely amazing hotel!
text: When I first arrived at the hotel I was worried because I needed an early check in but the front desk was very accommodating! On top of letting me check in early they upgraded my room to a suite which was beyond nice. The room itself was super spacious and very nicely decorated. Also, there was an expresso maker in the room which I loved. The staff I encountered were very helpful and welcoming and there was always someone at the front desk if you needed anything. The location was also ideal because you are in very close walking distance of so many attractions such as the louvre! I had an absolutely lovely time at the hotel and I will definitely be returning!

title: Fantastic stay
text: We had a fantastic stay. Top A location and great sevice. Overall, price/location/service are in perfect balance. Hotel Mayfair will definately be our place to stay in Paris for the next few years. Love it!

title: Rude Staff & Overall Disappointing Experince
text:
I recently stayed at Hotel Mayfair Paris and was shocked by the poor guest service. 
The staff was very rude and were showing a lot of attitude. This is INSANE, overall my stay was very disappointing and I don't recommend at all.

title: Rooms need to be updated
text: The hotel is cute and centrally located. Staff is friendly but the rooms and bathrooms are old and need renovation. Room service selection is limited and the food is a bit below average although breakfast is ok.

title: Disappointing Experience
text: After we booked our stay, France instituted (due to the COVID surge) a restriction on traveling from the UK into France. Since we were legally prohibited from traveling to Paris through no fault of our own, we asked the hotel to simply grant us credit to stay at the hotel on a future date after the travel restriction was lifted. The hotel kept the our entire payment for our three-night stay and would not allow us a credit. We have not experienced this with any other hotel, airline, etc. since the pandemic began and travel has had to be rescheduled due to restrictions. Needless to say, when were are able to travel to Paris we will stay at a hotel that does not exploit an awful situation to make some extra money just because they can technically get away with refusing any flexibility or understanding.

title: Charming Hotel in Perfect Location
text:
If you're looking for a boutique hotel that's close to many attractions - this place is it. You can easily walk to museums like the Louvre and Musee d'Orsay, and take a longer stroll to places like Ile Saint-Louis and the Marais neighborhood. High-end shopping is nearby, along with many restaurants and cafes. The Christmas market is almost at the hotel's doorstep, and you can walk over to the Champs-Elysees to see all the lights. Definitely worth a walk to see Notre Dame Cathedral plus a display about the renovations and also children's artwork. Really moving.

The Hotel Mayfair and my room itself were both very clean. While the double room isn't very large, it was doable for one person. Not much was happening in the bar area, but you could get a drink if you wanted. They may serve food there as well - not sure. The staff, though, were very nice and friendly throughout my stay.

Something to note as well - there is a pharmacy nearby on Rue Saint-Honore that can convert U.S. vaccination cards into the French health pass. Very quick and easy. I believe it was around 36 euros. They also do rapid antigen testing, and can email you the results in around a half hour or so. This was 25 euros.

Two more side notes, the taxi fare to and from the CDG airport is a set price at roughly 60 euros. And, there is a place to exchange $ right next door to the hotel.

Overall, I had a great stay in Paris and at the Hotel Mayfair. Would definitely visit again.

title: Would come back
text: Small hotel with Everything you need in a very good location. Staff  wonderful and helpful. Large clean rooms. With comfortable beds. Adequate fresh breakfast and close to metro. Very tastefully decorated like a little French palace. Lovely.

title: Good boutique hotel in the heart of Paris
text:
It’s a nice boutique hotel walking distance from Louvre, champ elessye and various other things. Metro stations are also close by, so are various good eateries and shopping areas.
Rooms are bigger than most hotels in Paris. Staff is helpful. However, it’s a small building inside a lane, so don’t expect great view. However it has very comfortable rooms

title: Perfect location!
text: A thoroughly wonderful stay, and the location could not have been more perfect, across the Tuilleries, next to the Place Concorde, walking distance the the Louvre, Rue Cambon and Place Vendome. The rooms were very clean and my room at the top floor had such a lovely view. Would definitely recommend and our thanks again to Aurelie and Eugenie. Looking forward to the next stay!

title: A hidden gem in Paris!
text: Lovely gem of a hotel in a very nice area of Paris. Our Junior Suite was very spacious by Paris standards and was well appointed and clean. The bathroom was very big with plenty of amenities. Easily accommodated 3 adults. Coffee was delivered very promptly each morning.

title: Lovely, Quaint Hotel- Great Location
text: This our third stay at the Mayfair and we still love it.  Beautiful little boutique hotel in a perfect location.  Walking distance to almost everything.  Very nice rooms, nice breakfast and very friendly staff.  As a boutique hotel, it does not have all of the amenities or services of larger hotels, but if you want quiet and quaint, this is a perfect location to explore Paris.  Very reasonably priced.  Well recommended for sure

title: Great visit with my parents at Mayfair!
text: Had a great stay at the Hotel Mayfair, would absolutely stay here again. Location is great - right next to the Tuileries, can walk to the Louvre, easy subway access via Concorde, convenient shopping nearby on Rue St Honore. Staff is very kind and helpful. Did not eat at the hotel as breakfast was not included with the room.

title: Exquisite
text:
Superb location, spotless, 5 star 
Would gladly come back . 
Reception Staff brilliant as was those who maintained the room . 
Beautifully appointed bedrooms and en suites. 
Location right opposite Touileries gardens.
Drinks at corner of street where hotel not cheap £12 for a beer , but I guess your in middle of a city . 
Highly recommend.

title: Disappointment
text:
Recently, my family and I booked Hotel Mayfair Paris for a stay in early April.  Unfortunately, due to the worldwide pandemic and our governments restricting travel between our countries, it was impossible for us to visit Paris and this hotel. 

While most every other hotel and airline is bending over backwards to accommodate traveler victims of the pandemic like our family of five, reservation manager, Florence Chertier, provided a pompous email response. On behalf of Hotel Mayfair, she informed us that they would not refund our +$1,000 USD for our two rooms, clearly letting us know that they would rather greatly profit on the backs of pandemic victims for no services rendered. Our reservation was in place for less than a few weeks and they had plenty of availability when we booked. They lost no business while they held our reservations for this short time. Furthermore, we called them immediately after the travel restrictions were announced, giving them a full month to reserve our two rooms. Knowing that they plan to pocket our $1,000 USD and likely reserve them again is unbelievable. 

Choosing to profit on the backs of victims during this worldwide panic, without doing anything to earn that +$1,000 of profit, is disgusting, heartless, and a perfect example of what not to do in business. 

TRAVELER BEWARE OF HOTEL MAYFAIR IN PARIS...DO NOT STAY AT THIS HOTEL!!!  We’d recommend you consider staying with luxury hotels that truly care about their travelers and have been showing compassion in this time of need like Marriott and Hyatt have done for us recently.

title: Great hotel on a great location!
text: The Mayfair hotel is just off Rue Rivoli, a great place to start exploring Paris. We had a junior suite and it was very good indeed. Plenty of space, a great big bed and 2 pillows each. Large bathroom with a tub wide enough to fit two easily. The staff is very helpful and the breakfast buffet really fills you up. Will be back next time we are in Paris.

title: Good services.
text:
We enjoyed our stay from 4.2.2020 to 9.2.2020.

The staff are very friendly and helpful. 
For instance, when we requested to chage our room to a room with standing shower as we are elderly person, the person in charge was trying her very best to help us for our request, 

Nice room and newly renovated. 

Strong recommendation. 

Guests from Singapore.

title: Mediocre hotel in good location, fair value
text: First impression was not great as there's a vague "oldy-musty" smell in the reception area and the staff is not too friendly, however the hotel is located in a good location which made the night rate quite acceptable for Paris. The view from my room was... a wall so that was not great but the bonus was it was quiet - rubbish clearance in the morning can be loud if you are on the street side where however you get the best views! The room itself was spacios, clean, bathroom was recently renovated with a large shower head. There isn't a restaurant within the hotel, but they provide room service, I was told by a restaurant nearby - if you are hungry and can't be bothered to go far, head to the L'Ardoise which is just a couple of minutes walk. Breakfast OK, nothing special but it offers anything from continental to cooked.

title: Just perfect
text:
what a brilliant recommendation, my friends told us about this place and decided to book there for my partner's birthday, its beautiful, clean, very close to everywhere we wanted to visit, including Louvre museum, the rooms are amazing and fully equipped, wifi was available too.
would highly recommend.

title: Comfortable, quiet in the middle of Vendome area
text: Great stay and lovely people.     It is a quiet place with perfect location.   Hop over to Ritz or to Le Meurice bars for an elegant cocktail hour.    You are within 5 min walk.    You absolutely can’t get any closer to Chanel unless you are in Coco’s sofa bed at her suite at the Ritz!    Comfy firm beds.    Not fancy but traditional Paris accommodation in a world class location.

title: Hotel Mayfair!
text: We stayed in the Hotel Mayfair for 2 nights.  The front desk employees were very nice and helpful, especially with transportation as we were there during the transportation strike.  The amenities of the hotel were well worth the cost of the room.  Bed was comfy and had nice bathrooms.  Really close to lots of the attractions of Paris.  Highly recommend giving it a try.

title: Great Experience at the Hotel Mayfair Paris
text: This is the 4th year in a row that we have stayed at the Mayfair.  It is a bueautiful hotel with a friendly and supportive staff. We arrived in Paris with no idea of the pending transportation strike.  It caused us to change our entire trip and the staff was very helpful in making those changes. The hotel recently updated the rooms on at least 3 floors making them even more bueatiful and modern.  The hotel is centrally located for museums and shopping.  Within walking distance of major attractions. The breakfast buffet is filled with European and American breakfast items.  Highly recommend you consider this hotel.

title: Gorgeous boutique hotel, super friendly staff
text:
The Mayfair is a very beautifully appointed boutique hotel in the very city center of Paris, just around the corner of Place Vendôme. A great location for the Louvre, the Tuileries and other sights. And shopping of course! Metro Station Concorde can be reached in 2 minutes.
The room I had was quite spacious, with very beautiful furniture, a big bathroom and a coffee machine. There was also a very good assortment of cold beverages in the mini bar, ranging from water over soft drinks to wine and champagne.
The whole hotel is well maintained and very clean. They also have a sustainability initiative which is simply great.
The staff is exceptionally friendly and super helpful. I had a wine in the hotel bar one evening and the bar tender was so nice and even turned on some lights for me to be better able to read. The receptionist recommended a great restaurant for dinner (Flottes, also around the corner, great food, nice people). I had to leave a day early due to unforeseen strike disruptions, and although I only returned to the hotel around lunchtime to fetch my luggage, the lady in charge didn‘t let me pay for the 3rd night which was very generous. She also canceled my taxi reservation for the next morning and suffered through an annoying phone call with the taxi company on my behalf. I couldn‘t have been received any better and I am amazed by the hotel itself as well as the people working there. Many thanks for making me feel so welcome. I‘ll be sure to return! Merci beaucoup pour votre hospitalité! Vive le Mayfair!

title: Great Place to Stay
text: We stayed here four nights prior to our river cruise. The staff was great! Breakfast was wonderful and included in our stay, not just continental which is what we are used to in the states, but what we could order our egg style! Boutique style of stay meaning small, personable and warm setting. Conveniently located if you are wanting to stay in heart of Paris.

title: Excellent location
text: Great staff and breakfast, Paris 1, walking distance to all major attractions, renovated rooms on the higher floors. As in many old buildings you can hear if a neighbor decides to have a shower late at night. Very loud noise from the pipes. Thank God it only happened once !

title: Good placement, Old fashioned hotel
text:
We came here in October 2019. Check in was smooth and we got help with our bags up to our room. The newly renovated room was good, not great, but good. Bed was very hard but we slept like babies the whole trip (Maybe because of the 20.000+ steps we took walking around Paris). The Hotel is located close to everything since it's walking distance to the high fashion shopping and also the subway if you want to go elsewhere. I liked the old fashioned feeling on the hotel, but i think it was a bit over prices and it really annoyed me that you "had" to leave your key in the reception when you left and even though they changed staff in the lobby you could just say a number and get a key. We even got the wrong key once.

To summeroize: Great location, an good hotel but leaving the key feels outdated and not so safe.

title: Nice hotel in great location
text: We stayed at the Hotel Mayfair Paris for 5 nights last week in a renovated, deluxe room.  The hotel is ideally situated - around the corner from the beautiful Tuileries Gardens, walking distance to the Louvre and other main sites and easy to reach the Seine and Left Bank.  The renovated rooms are spacious and nicely appointed.  The staff, especially Leticia at the front desk and Ronnie the bellman, are very friendly and helpful.  Our only complaints were that they don’t offer water or coffee machine in room (minor issues) and that the bed is unbelievably hard (major issue)- so much so that we both awoke each day with terrible pain in our shoulders, hips and back.   It was so bad that as much as we enjoyed other aspects of the hotel, I’m not sure we can stay there again.  Perhaps if they upgrade the mattresses along with the room decor.

title: Last Night in Paris
text:
We stayed here for one night at the end of our Europe trip and it was such a nice area to have one last wander through Paris. The gardens are basically right across the street and there are two metro stations within a short walk. We walked maybe 5 minutes to the bridge across from the Place de la Concorde to watch the Eiffel Tower glitter at night which was lovely. The staff was very kind and welcoming. After we checked in they carried my bag to our room and showed us around. We picked the cheapest option to stay but our room was massive. If the small European rooms bother you, this would be the place to stay. The bathroom was very big and there was basically a small living room area before you reached your room. It actually was the perfect set up for us to completely dump out our bags and repack them for our flight home. 

This was a really awesome hotel. I was very sad we only had one night with them!

title: Excellent Staff!
text: Although we only spent one night in Paris, we had a wonderful experience at the Mayfair! The hotel is cozy and feels like home, decorated in classic Parian style, and is in a great location. The room and bathroom were big and comfortable. The most incredible thing about this hotel is the staff. Everyone was friendly, welcoming and very helpful. But the absolute best thing about this hotel is Lucian! (I hope I spelled his name correctly!) On the way to the airport, we realized we had left our passports in the safe. Lucian did not hesitate, and was kind enough to personally deliver them to us at the airport. If it were not for him, we would have missed our flight home! Thank you again, we cannot say it enough! We would definitely stay there again!

title: Wonderful Hotel!
text: Hotel Mayfair welcomed us to Paris with open arms!  Our room was a spacious and comfortable mix of the new and old with a modern bathroom.  The hotel staff was gracious and helpful, and the location was perfect for us.  We thoroughly enjoyed our stay and highly recommend this hotel.

title: Paris for Fashion Week
text: Love this hotel!  Great location, charming rooms, excellent (and fast) room service and cordial staff.  Also in a very central location near the Louvre and a quick walk to the Musee d Orsay, Eiffel Tower, etc.  I felt very safe day and night in this area.  Met and exceeded all expectations.

title: Paris Gem
text: We spent 5 nights In Paris at the Mayfair. Very charming decor. Pleasant and helpful staff. You cannot beat the location. It’s within walking distance of many things and short cab rides to other things. Had a very pleasant stay.

title: Great staff and location
text: Every person I came into contact with at the Hotel Mayfair, from the registration desk to housekeeping to the lady in the breakfast room,  was very,  very welcoming and friendly.  Most spoke English or understood my rudimentary French.  The room, although tiny and lacking a view, was perfect for me as it was quiet and decorated well. I slept like a log! Excellent location, close to the Louvre and the Metro. I will stay there again,  for sure!

title: Excellent. Central position, comfortable, safe and competitive fees.
text: I was hosted at Mayfair in February 2019, for business in Paris. Mayfair has enviable central position: just few minutes walk to Place de la Concorde and metro station. The hotel is comfortable, the staff is friendly; it is safe due to good video surveillance at the reception floor and in each corridor of each floor. The room are clean, quiet and comfortable. Breakfast is available with extra fee: it is good, served in a quiet room with a helping person if needed. A good restaurant is available just side by side the hotel with fair prices, considering its central position. I would advice this hotel both for business travel and for holidays with the family or your partner.

title: Weekend in Paris
text: The hotel has maintained an authentic decor from the past. We were pleasantly surprised to be upgraded to a suite. The space (living room/bedroom/bathroom) was large compared to previous hotels in Paris that I’ve stayed in. Bathroom has both shower and huge bathtub. Elevator exits. The front desk folks were extremely helpful giving advise on whatever we asked about. Breakfast was available and tasty. The location was perfect, close to the metro, dining, park, and general site seeing in District 1! The area was safe. We walked 5 min late at night to see the the “sparkling” Eiffel Tower.

title: Great Boutique Hotel
text: The Hotel Mayfair was in an excellent location. It was walking distance from a lot of main attractions in Paris. The staff was friendly and helpful. The rooms were very nice, but a little on the small side (We had the superior room). The only complaint I had was when we locked the deadbolt, we unable to unlock it, and were stuck in the room till the hotel staff came. This happened twice and I was told it would be fixed. I’m not sure if it ever got fixed because I had to catch an early morning flight and didn’t lock the deadbolt just in case we got locked in the room again. All in all, I would recommend this hotel as it’s a great place to stay!

title: A nice hotel at the right place
text:
The hotel is nice as well as its service. 
Close to the main attractions but the steet itself is rather silent. 

We spent here a few nights during our business trip and it was a good choice. 
The rooms are small but it’s normal in this area.

title: Excellent!
text: This hotel is in a nice location, clean, with great amenities, but the staff are superior. Special thanks to Florence who went out of her way to accommodate us after we found out we had to stay an extra two days. Not only did she make room for us, but she let us stay in our room. They were fully booked, but made room for us anyway, so we'll be going back, over and over and over again. Highly recommended!

title: Five Star Treatment
text: We had a great stay the cleaning staff and front desk staff were excellent. The hotel is centrally located withing easy walking distance to the Louvre, the Seine River, and Champs-Elysees. The rooms and facilities were clean and the staff professional and courteous, even patient in helping me with my French. The last day we were charged for the full breakfast instead of the buffet, other than that, we had a very good time. Be aware of pickpockets, scam artists, and younger age groups of teens targeting tourists.

title: Rude and unkind staff
text: I saw a horrible scene in this hotel today. A tour guide coming to greet her clients was rudely refused access to toilets here... even though her clients were staying at the hotel. The receptionist was an absolute clod. She ran after the guide as though she were some kind of common criminal! What kind of world does the Mayfair believe it’s living in? Toilets are a human right and no one deserves to be treated the way this poor lady just doing her job was. I was so offended, I decided to tell all of my friends and clients to never use this mediocre-at-best hotel. In the world of Airbnb, there is no need for this rude behaviour. Run far, far away from this place

title: 5 nights in Paris
text: Great hotel well located, we booked a larger room as we where there for 5 nights early July. Helpful reception staff & great cleaning staff, room was always clean upon our return each day. Easy access to all Paris has to offer. Would recommend if staying in Paris.

title: Excellent
text: Hotel Mayfair was perfect in every way. The location is very central and within walking distance of quite a few of the places that people usually want to visit while in Paris. The rooms are not very big but beautifully decorated. The staff are extremely friendly and helpful. Would definitely stay here again.

title: Jewel is the gem of Hotel
text: This hotel was fantastic. Jewel is a porter who will do anything to help you. The director of reception was especially helpful in moving our room where the AC worked better. A little boutique hotel with a big heart in the 1st district where we can walk everywhere.

title: Best Boutique Hotel in Paris
text: My friend and I stayed five nights at the Hotel Mayfair.  This is our second stay, and for good reason.  The front desk staff is personable, professional, and ready to help with dinner reservations or calling taxis.  Breakfast is a real treat, as the coffee is excellent, and you can have an omelette customized with mushrooms, cheese, or veggies!  You choose!  The location of this hotel is walking distance from the Louvre, Tuileries, the Seine, or high end shopping if you so choose. The third floor of the hotel has been completely redecorated, and the rooms are gorgeous.  Maxim, front desk clerk, helped make our stay so very enjoyable by suggesting restaurants nearby when we arrived tired and jet lagged.  We will return!

title: Our only night in Paris !
text: A friend recommend the Mayfair for many reasons; location, first class decor and incredible helpful staff who spoke perfect English! I asked for the closest pharmacy and Aissata provide a map highlighting the way. So kind and friendly. Location is between Place Vendome and across from the Tullieres Gardens. We had a picnic there with a bottle of wine under the shady trees. The staff really know how to make your Paris dreams come true!

title: Great small hotel in a great location
text: Fourth time staying at the Mayfair. Beautiful new renovations.  Best location in Paris on Rue Rivoli between the Louvre and Place Concord and across the street from the Concord Metro stop. Small rooms, but totally efficient and beautifully decorated. Great service, a full bar and breakfast and room service available.

title: Paris Visit
text: Solid Hotel for the the price in a great location. Walking distance to the louvre, tuileries, champs-elysees, fashion district, and place de la concorde. Lots to do in the neighborhood. The hotel has old world charm. Beds were comfortable. Only negative thing I have to say is the bar and restaurant is very limited. Breakfast is continental. We would go next door to the Westin for breakfast every morning.

title: Best deal in Paris Hotel
text: Perfect location in Paris, near the Louvre and Place de la Concorde.  Nightly prices can often be found for less than $200, unheard of for 4 star hotels in Paris.  Many rooms have now been renovated, although quite small, as is usual for Paris hotels, and many have balconies overlooking Rue Rouget de Lisle.  Breakfast is good but pricey at 15 euros for Continental and 25 euros for full breakfast, but cheaper alternatives can be found a short walk down Rue de Rivoli.  The staff is friendly and helpful in case any problem arises.

title: Superb location and friendly staff
text: Loved the location, next to jardin de tuilières, so close to louvre and in a very lively neighborhood. The staff at the front desk was also very good and accommodating, seeing that we are with a kid, they immediately upgraded us to a superior room. The rooms are spacious and have everything that you may need for a comfortable stay. And the reception people are happy to assist for everything else. Had a very pleasant stay.

title: Wonderful Hotel / great location
text:
Spent four nights at this lovely hotel.  Everything was perfect. We had a very nice room on the 5th floor. Hotel staff was all so very nice. They suggested restaurants and other areas of Paris that we might find interesting.

This hotel is in a great location. Walking distance to the Louvre; close to the Museo de Orsey; across from a wonderful park, Tuileries Garden. Short metro ride to Champs-Elysees. 

The hotel staff is wonderful. Do everything they can to make your stay comfortable. On their recommendation, we took the Metro to Bastille and got to experience another area of Paris. Julian at the front desk recommended a wonderful French restaurant, and the food was excellent. My best meal in Paris. I wish I had asked for his recommendation sooner. I would have had all my dinners here.
I hope to return in the near future. Thank you everyone at Hotel Mayfair for a wonderful stay.

title: excellent hotel
text: we stayed here over the easter period and although it was expensive it was worth every penny . we almost cancelled after the notre dame fire but so glad we didnt . Great city , great hotel and the location was fantastic - close to everything , walking or on the metro . Very safe area too with some lovely restaurants just round the corner. looking forward to coming here again

title: Best location but room needs updating
text:
Stayed 2 nights here before flying to Stockholm.  Because we did not have a lot of time in Paris,  I decided to book the best located hotel so that we would not waste time travelling around the city.  I was certainly right about that as we were steps from Place Vendome,  Tuileries,  the Louvre,  and a 20 minute walk to the Eiffel Tower.

We,  however,  got a still unrenovated room and although the room itself was big and good Parisian style decor (we got a family room) the carpet certainly needed updating.  Plus when the made the sofa into a bed,  you had to squeeze to get to the bedroom.  
My daughter also didn't like the temp controls of the shower (2 valves and not a mixer) although I myself did not have a problem with it.  

We stayed out our first night (came back at past midnight). and thought we got locked out.  The entrance was closed and it took a few minutes for someone to buzz us in. Ask about that if you plan to stay out late.

 I'd consider staying here again if I get a newly renovated room as this hotel is not cheap

title: Beware of Front Desk Manager
text: The hotel is in an excellent location and that is what you pay for. The rooms are nicely furnished and the area is close to everything. I had an issue with housekeeping entering my room even though I had the do not disturb sign displayed. My toiletries were thrown away and needed to be replaced. I brought this to the attention of the front desk. At the start, the front desk manager displayed an attitude of not wanting to help. All she could say was "I'm sorry." The reception manager would not give me the contact information for hotel management so that I could discuss this with them. I paid over $200.00 per night for this. Not worth it. Paris is a beautiful city and has wonderful other hotels and I will stay at another hotel when I visit again.

title: Mrs Cheryl Mew
text: Spent 4 nights at this beautiful boutique hotel. Great breakfast and very good service. Highly recommended. Very good breakfast. Staff were great, very helpful. Hotel was centrally situated, easy access to the underground as well.

title: Great Boutique Hotel
text: We stayed 5 nights at the hotel.  It's in a great location, close to the Louvre and D'Orsay.  We were on the 6th floor and even though the hotel is undergoing renovations, it did not bother us at all.  They started from the top and were working on floor 3 when we left.  Our room had 3 terrace windows (including 1 in the bathroom).  My only complaint is that we could not shut the radiator off and it was constantly blowing heat.  The duvet covers are heavy and we would find ourselves having to open the terrace doors.  Fine at night, but with the doors open you could hear the French police car sirens.  The staff were very friendly and we thought the price was great.

title: Lovely Hotel
text:
We normally like to stay around St. Honore so we chose Mayfair Hotel this time to compare it with the other hotels we have stayed in around the area. 

The room we got (#24 corner, highly recommended) was bigger than any of the rooms from the other hotels we have stayed in. The front office and concierge were all very nice and the food was worth it. 

This is our new go to hotel in St. Honore

title: Perfect Winter Vacation
text: We arrived at the Hotel Mayfair bright and early on a Sunday morning, they were very welcoming and the hotel lobby was beautiful!  Unfortunately, we had to wait a few hours for our room because check in is 2:00PM.  Note: When traveling over seas book your room from the night before!  Lesson learned!  Even though, they made us very comfortable and we were able to get in our room by noonish.  We were upgraded to a junior suite, which was lovely.  Very european, loved it!  The front desk staff was very helpful with directions, tickets to different venues, dinner recommendations and general info about Paris.  I would highly recommend this hotel, close to everything and just perfect!

title: Solid, but feel like we could have done better for the $$
text: First the good - a great location in the 1st (if you want to be right next to the Tuileries, Louvre, D'Orsay and a good subway stop) and the bathroom was EPIC.  Nice, warm marble floors and nice bathtub.  The room itself has that old furniture, ratty wallpaper, musty smell, but then again so do a lot of older hotels in Europe.  The Wifi and cable were super spotty, but not a deal breaker for me since this was a vacation.  Not sure it's worth a return visit, because while the location was good, it's very touristy, with little going on at night; no good neighborhood boites to get a small bite and the place becomes quiet.  Next time, I'll try a less touristy location in more of a neighborhood location.

title: Great staff, but pricey for what you get
text: We found the staff to be friendly and helpful - a real selling point for the place. On the downside, the rooms felt a little tired and could do with a facelift (particularly for what we paid to stay there). Overall, it compared favorably to other places we've stayed in Paris (particularly Novotel, les Halles), but that's another story.

title: Frissons of danger
text:
With an extremely attractive room rate for a five-star location, we wouldn't let some construction sounds as the floor above was renovated bother us.  And it didn't.  The hammering and sawing never began before 9:45am and always finished by tea time.  The room, which the hotel upgraded to deluxe size, was large and comfortable, the staff charming and willing to help and the ancient elevator, with room for no more than one traveller of Trumpian proportions a magnet for all kids in the group.  Just don't touch the doors.  Be patient: they swing open on their own.
The sound that prompted the frissons of danger began late Friday afternoon as all local merchants without steel shutters had heavy plywood installed over their storefront windows.  The sound of sirens wailing down rue de Rivoli continued through the night as the riot police and the national guard took their positions. 
We left the hotel at 7:30am, an hour before dawn for the 40 minute walk to the nearest open Metro station.  We passed through phalanxes of police and demonstrators who held an uneasy truce until the sun rose.  By the time all hell broke loose, we were on the train heading to CDG with wonderful stories.  Thank you Hotel Mayfair.

title: Exhibition/Museum Visit
text:
Loved it small but very nice hotel ideally situated in the centre of Paris Premier Arridossment location just close to everything 

Hotel staff superb nice little bar and room was tasteful Victorian style Reception speak English 

One major problem after visiting the Centre de Pompidou we walked right into the clash between Gilet Jaunes riot and the police As we walked into the street that led to our hotel there was a police baton charge  towards us in the street we had run out onto Rue de Ravoli opposite Taruilles Gardens it was a mess people pulling out the park failings a car on fire. For security reasons the hotel and houses had turned off all the lights in the street the hotel was in we went back still cars burning in the area we we were faced with another charge and CS gas was deployed over towards the park my eyes started to smart in the ensuing chaos I couldn’t find the hotel in the dark it was very scary indeed. Eventually found it and went back out for dinner later around 9pm it was calm but a shop had been looted bricks on the pavement Hotel guided me to an area that restaurants would be open away from this area The next day I sent to Musse d’Oray across the park walkway bridge over the adrien not that far it was a miracle overnight everything had been tied up. 
The staff were very helpful once I managed to get back to the hotel

Would I come again definitely

title: Cosy hotel
text: Centrally located to main interesting touristy and shopping places. highlights is the lourve that is a few blocks away. rooms are nice and comfortable. very responsive and accommodating front desk  team.

title: Perfect location
text:
Stayed for business recently, all hotel rooms in central Paris are expensive and this hotel is no different , staff were nice and hotel was clean and comfortable, 

Right in the central area and within easy walking distance of many of the big ticket sights , Eiffel Tower , lourve etc , very pricey for food so we ate out at cafes etc , restaurant cafe next door where a coke was €10 and a pint of beer was €14 !! Found places closer to the tower were actually better value ... however this hotel is a great spot for touring about Paris and is very comfortable, as long as your prepared for nothing cheap Paris is a wonderful city and this hotel is right in the centre of it ...

title: Everything else was nice but an item was stolen from my room
text:
The hotel was nice for its price, good breakfast, it didn't smell mold which is common problem in Paris. Hotel was also clean and the location is very good.

One thing can make it pretty bad though. I forgot my expensive scarf in my room which I noticed after check-out. I made a phone call to the hotel and sent couple of emails requesting it but it was not found. The only conclusion to this is that it was stolen and I'm 100 % sure that it was left in the room. What a shame.

title: Mayfare is charming
text: Such a dainty and good location. Good staff and very friendly English speaking teams to take care of guests. Highly recommended for stay on buz or pleasure. The location is surrounded by great restaurants and souvenirs shops. Plus most of the big tourist areas are a walk away.

title: Great location and
text:
Location of the hotel was ideal, close to The Louvre and the reasonably distance to the champs elyss shopping area. The hotel room itself was clean, tidy and spacious, so no complaint. 

The staff was very polite, helpful and spoke English well, so a big plus. 

The 2 negatives are 1. having the need to hand over room key (physically key) everything you leave the hotel premise and ask for it back when you return, so it’s bit annoying. 2. Initial check in, there was confusion in that the room was booked only for 1 person meaning single bed for a couple.. So had to fork out more for what we thought was 1 room = either 2 twin or 1 double bed. 

Overall good experience at the hotel and recommend it for short stay!

title: Small, comfortable, well situated hotel
text: This is a well placed hotel about 5 minutes walk from Gare du Nord. The room was small but comfortable,  there was no noise (my room faced the courtyard), and the bathroom was well equipped as well. There was breakfast available but I did not try this. There are quite a few restaurants and cafes nearby, and you. An walk down (mostly downhill!) to the Louvre in about 40 minutes. It’s a good place from which to explore Paris, and also for a short stay if you have a train to catch the next day.

title: Avoid this hotel, they don’t understand the meaning of hospitality

The rooms are exceptionally small and even the passages and lift (elevator) seem to be smaller than would seem to be legally permissible. The real issue for me though was that I needed some minor assistance with the storage of a bag whilst I attended an important meeting in London. This really would have been no inconvenience and I even offered to pay. Unfortunately the concierge repeatedly refused to help with a series of weak excuses and in full knowledge that this would ruin my whole trip. I honestly can’t think of an example where I have met a less empathetic person in a service industry. His excuses were so pointless one can only draw the conclusion that he actually relished ruining my trip. I have had so many amazing experiences in France, and in Paris in particular, with warm, kind and helpful people and I love traveling to France for this reason. This hotel is definitely the exception to this rule.

text:

title: Weekend break
text:
We just returned from a short breat in France, where I choose to stay at the Libertel 
It’s only a 4or 5 minute walk from the gare du nord station so was perfect 
The staff on reception were great friendly & helpful in every way
It is a very busy area, lot of hustle & bustle but wasn’t aware of this when inside the hotel very clean & peaceful hotel, while our room did seem a lot smaller than on the photos, nevertheless it was big enough

All we needed really
There is a little market across the road full of local sausage cheese bread etc , browsed it on Sunday very excited to go back to buy on the Monday only to find it was shut, missed out there I feel

There’s plenty of options to eat/drink within less than 5 minutes walk from the hotel in all directions 
We had a glorious meal at Maison bleue local food & wine 👍🏻

We visited champs Elyse which was a 15 minute taxi drive, well worth it

All in all a great experience & a nice little hotel

title: Libertel but no Liberty
text:
This was my second stay with Libertel Gare du Nord, the first one was a short pleasant single night stay in 2019 but this one was the exact opposite. 

As other travelers have noticed, the rooms at Libertel are really really tiny. They offer three kinds of rooms: Cozy (85 m2), Comfort (115 m2) and Superior (135 m2), I purposefully got the comfort as i didn't want to feel claustrophobic during my stay. However even the comfort rooms are really cramped - it is difficult to walk without bumping into the bed and there are absolutely no drawers to store your luggage or stuff. You cant even fully pull out the study chair so I am not sure why it is even there. The only amenity in the room is a kettle which I am sure is from the 1990s.

The bathrooms are tiny too, with doors not closing fully and the pot directly facing the bed.  The management also cheapens out with the cosmetics as only a 3-in-1 body, hair, bath gel is placed in the bathroom. The towels are absolutely paper thin. Thankfully I was a single person in a double room so I could use the two towels to dry myself off properly.

The tiny trend continues with the corridors, which are so narrow that two people cant even walk together. The rooms end up being so close that every time someone enters/exits, it becomes really loud. The loud elevator's bangs don't help either.

I would have managed and not complained if it was just about the small rooms, but these features were accompanied by horrible room cleaning service and a breakfast spread that I am pretty sure breaks some kind of law.

When my room was cleaned, none of the basic necessities like soap, toilet paper were renewed and the toilet was still dirty. Realizing this, I had to go down to the reception at 11pm to get some more toilet paper. 

Also, the hotel advertises a great 10euro breakfast and publicizes the same with a long list. I made my own list containing things that were missing from their spread: Fresh Fruits, Homemade cakes, Boiled Eggs, Madeleines, pastries and Bread. The fruits and the eggs were a big deal for me so when I asked the restaurant-lady for them, she rudely replied that she didn't have any eggs and gave me two rotten apples that I threw immediately (wish I had taken a photo of them). This honestly borders on misleading and fraudulent advertisement.

A few positives though: the receptionists were always helpful and cheerful. They even printed out my passenger locator form for my return. Also, the location is amazing for anyone traveling to/from Gare du Nord but is quite far from the main tourist attractions.  There are many supermarkets, restaurants, cafes in the vicinity though and the beautiful Montmartre is also a short walk away. The room is well lighted and has several sockets as well. The windows are amazingly 100% soundproof blocking out all the noise from the busy roads outside.

During my time at Libertel, I can honestly say that I didn't have any liberty to move around my room, to eat well or to bathe well. Au revoir pour toujours.

title: Libertel Gare du Nord Suede hotel
text:
We stayed at this hotel for three nights. It’s 5 mins walk from the main train station which is the station for Eurostar. Hotel room was quite small but ok for two people sharing. Great bed and great shower room. Very clean. 
Room had basic tea and coffee facilities. Fitted hairdryer in the shower room. 
Only criticism was the cup in the room had a crack and was not replaced. 
Breakfast was basic and cost 10 euro per person.

text:

It was very quiet and spotless, cleanest hotel room I’ve stayed in, of any hotel class, in a very long time.   

The location, one block straight on from Gare du Nord, was perfect for our late arrival and early departure via Eurostar.   The street from the station to the hotel has wonderful bakeries and several restaurants.  The area is typically of what you will find near any large train station so we didn’t venture very far from our path and decided to take Taxis back when we were coming in late.

Tip for quick trip tourists, the Big Bus Hop-on/off bus stop is just a block away.   We bought a deluxe 2 day pass with boat tour on the first bus that leaves Gare du Nord at 9:05 and used it as our sole tour transportation for the two days we were in Paris, other than taxis home after dark.   It worked well buses were frequent many with live commentary.  The last bus returns around 8:00pm.

title: Tiny room but convenient location
text:
LOCATION:
Really near Gare Du Nord train station. We managed to walk there to and fro with our two heavy 28" luggage. 
There are convenience stores (though not open 24 hours) and bakeries along the walk from hotel to station. 

ROOM: 
(Type - Superior Double)
We got a high floor quiet facing room with a view, as per our request. It was street-facing but not noisy at all. 

Size wasn't luxurious -- walking space was compromised once we opened up both our luggage on the floor.

It was two single beds joined together. Would have preferred a proper queen or king bed so that there would not be a gap between the beds after some movements.

Room comes with necessities like safe, mini fridge and coffee maker. 

This room is more suitable for couples really, because of the configuration and design of the bathroom. The sliding door design means that when you're on the toilet seat, you can actually see anyone outside the bathroom from wide gap between the sliding doors. And be seen as well. Would be better with bathroom doors that give better privacy. 

Apart from that, we liked the big shower area and good water pressure. Heating rods inside the bathroom worked really well, which is useful for doing small pieces of laundry during our winter stay. 

SERVICE:
Service from the receptionists were commendable. They'd always greet the guests leaving and entering through the doors.

title: Tiny room but great location
text:
We arrived at this hotel after dark. The reception staff was welcoming, helpful and efficient. Staff gave good advice about where we could and should not go during the gilets jaunes protest. 
The room was tiny but clean. We didn’t need a lot of space since we were not planning on being in the room very much. However, my husband who is a big guy had to turn sideways to get into and out of the bathroom. In addition, there was a problem with the drainage in the very shallow shower stall so, during each shower, I had to shut off the water a few times to allow it to drain or else the water would spill onto the floor. The toilet was in a separate room with a sliding door. One plus was that there was small safe to store valuables.
The buffet breakfast was adequate for the good price (10 euro) and the staff there was helpful. 
There were many sirens going by at night (we had a room with a street view) so, if you are a light sleeper, this could end up being very annoying. The blackout curtains were great.
The hotel is located near many restaurants so there were options for lunch and dinner and also for breakfast. It was about 5 minutes walk from the Gare du Nord station, provided you found and exited through the front entrance of the train station (which we did not the first time). Overall, we would stay here again but would find out if they have bigger bathrooms in any of the units.

title: Tiny room but served its purpose
text: I often advise people that rooms in Europe are basically smaller than those in the U.S. although rooms in large cities such as NYC can also be smaller than many others. I also advise that if you are worried about room size for a single person or dedicated couple you might need to stay home because you should not be seeing much of your room on a vacation.My room at this property even put me to the test. I chose the hotel as I wanted something near the Gare Nord upon returning from Germany. The hotel had a decent rating and the price was very low. Turns out the hotel has rooms ranging from 10' by 10' up to much larger. As I expected my good prize got a smaller room. The bed was shoved against a wall so the person against the wall had to either crawl over the other person or climb to the end of the bed. No closet but some pegs to hang your clothes on. A small desk was in the room. The bathroom was also tidy but functional, a shower, the smallest sink I've ever seen and a toilet. After all what do you need? To further show the room size the bathroom had a sliding door closing it off from the bedroom. No way a door would have opened outward and not hit the bed. A small area by some clothes pegs did provide space to store our two large suitcases. A very small TV was located in the wall where the bed was up against the wall. It would swivel out for watching. On the plus side, the property was very clean, the desk staff was friendly and knowledgeable, and several eating places and shops were nearby. The hotel served a buffet breakfast but we did not try it. I might stay here again for no more than a night if I was catching a train out of the Gard Nord but not for my general Paris stay. Of course a larger room choice would certainly have cured some of my problems with the hotel,
